chunks.text:
[DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1) > cBTC, cUSD and tETH]
Unlike TAC, cBTC and cUSD are pool-minted, not Bitcoin-issued: neither has a `T_CETCH` genesis, and
neither has been unwrapped to its public ERC-20 form yet — `tacBTC`
([`0xdf1d99148bEb7a9AFf1d95C49B3d22b7ed90D696`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xdf1d99148bEb7a9AFf1d95C49B3d22b7ed90D696))
and `tacUSD`
([`0x23cACFFAc2674514A6d4F6cD420B4cc2aC921564`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x23cACFFAc2674514A6d4F6cD420B4cc2aC921564))
both read `totalSupply() == 0` on mainnet today, so what's minted so far lives entirely as confidential
pool notes. Icons: [`cbtc-zk-icon.svg`](../contracts/tokenlist-drafts/cbtc-zk-icon.svg) and
[`cusd-zk-icon.svg`](../contracts/tokenlist-drafts/cusd-zk-icon.svg), standalone marks distinct from the
composite cBTC/TAC and cUSD/TAC pairing icons elsewhere in `contracts/`.

**cBTC** mints against real Bitcoin locks ([SPEC §5.7](../SPEC.md#57-cdp-cusd-and-cbtc)): `cbtcBackingSats()`
on the pool — the reflection-attested sum of live self-custody lock sats — read **4,800 sats** on 2026-09-28
(`cast call` against the live pool). A lock mints cBTC only once its 1.5× wstETH escrow clears; an
under-escrowed lock stays unmintable.

chunks.title: DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1) > cBTC, cUSD and tETH
chunks.text:
[DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1) > cBTC, cUSD and tETH]
**cUSD** mints as CDP debt against cBTC collateral, at the same 150% mint / 130% liquidation thresholds
([SPEC §5.7](../SPEC.md#57-cdp-cusd-and-cbtc)). `CollateralEngine.outstandingCusd()` read
**49,815,650** (in-system units) on 2026-09-28 across the engine's two currently-open positions; the insurance reserve is
still empty (nothing has ever been liquidated). Three real `CdpMinted` mints and one `CdpClosed` close, all
on the current engine:
[`0xb4a1f32d…afa7d4908`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0xb4a1f32d80ff1cd413d58023811eaafa8aed3388d3fa82741f52f06afa7d4908),
[`0x6da330c1…ebceaccb479b3229`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x6da330c161f236030ef83ce5c9c77268c735a52e7f9789c7ebceaccb479b3229)
(open), [`0x23851ea3…14e44232e`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x23851ea3ec4c0434940a1120505b0efe1878023e3d6faac9cea41ad14e44232e)
(closed), [`0x5f20ec5c…ffe52ec`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x5f20ec5cc1dc1ecd31cd8f60970e8947ca61165500dbb4cb27bb9c048ffe52ec)
(open).

**tETH** is not a separate asset from cETH — it's the same shared asset id
(`0x3cba71e1…03126f34`, [SPEC §4.2](../SPEC.md#42-assets-and-units)) named by chain context: "cETH" when
you're wrapping native ETH into the pool from Ethereum, "tETH" when the same note is spent on Bitcoin.
There's no bridge or swap between the two names, and no separate tETH ERC-20 — one note, read either way.
It has its own standalone Bitcoin-side mark: [`teth.svg`](../contracts/teth.svg) /
[`teth-icon.svg`](../contracts/teth-icon.svg), a "T" in Ethereum's brand purple. It's the asset the
[Bitcoin-native AMM pool](#bitcoin-native-amm-pool) actually trades: its founding reserves are tETH against
TAC.

What [key-only recovery](./RECOVERY.md) reads besides the pool's note events.

| Read | Value |

| `Wrap(depositId, assetId, amount)` | pool event; deposit ids matched to the wallet's derived wrap notes |

immutable SP1 Groth16 verifier, not the upgradeable gateway. Its reflection state starts from an attested
Bitcoin digest at the anchor height above.

chunks.title: DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Lineage
chunks.text:
[DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Lineage]
A `ConfidentialPool` cannot be upgraded. The protocol evolves by deploying a successor that users opt into by
exiting one pool and entering the next ([SPEC §8](../SPEC.md#8-deployment-lineage)). The current pool is the
root of its lineage.

- **Isolation.** Each pool's claim state (nullifiers, bridge mints, fast-lane consumes, cBTC locks and roots)
  is local to that contract. Every proof is bound to `chainId ‖ pool address`, and canonical tokens are
  addressed by their minter. A look-alike pool deployed by anyone else cannot spend this pool's escrow, mint
  its tokens or write its state; users should transact only with the addresses above.
- **One pool takes new value.** Setting `successor` closes this pool to new value, so at most one pool per
  lineage accepts it at a time.

chunks.title: DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Lineage > The lineage steward
chunks.text:
[DEPLOYMENTS.md > Deployed contracts > Lineage > The lineage steward]
The steward's entry point is `createNextGen(initCode, salt)`. Only the pool's immutable
`LINEAGE_STEWARD` (the ops multisig above) can call it, and only once. It deploys the successor from the
pool's own address and records it as `successor`, and that is the whole of its authority: the steward
chooses the successor's code and nothing else. `pool.successor()` reads zero while this pool is active. When
it is set, the pool emits `GenerationRetired(successor)`.

Once `successor` is set, the pool closes to new value:

- **Refused:** wraps of external assets, swaps, liquidity adds, cBTC mints, new CDP positions, farm bonds
  and surplus draws, public-AMM entry, farm funding, and any spend of a Bitcoin-homed note.
- **Still open:** every exit and every release of value already committed. That covers unwraps and
  transfers, liquidity removals, position closes, top-ups and liquidations, farm harvests, stealth and
  adaptor claims and refunds, deposits already escrowed, mints of Bitcoin burns that targeted this pool,
  and burning its own canonical token back into a note.
- **Cross-outs** reopen once the pool has written its handoff record, at its first attest after
  retirement. Its Bitcoin reflection stays open throughout.

The steward cannot touch escrow, freeze an exit, redirect a payout or set `successor` a second time.

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM]
One set of reserves, two ways to trade it. A swap or a liquidity position can be **public**, a plain Ethereum
transaction with no proof, or **private**, a note and a proof. Both move the same pool, so liquidity is never
split between them.

The app: [tacit.finance](https://tacit.finance/#card=swap), the front page's Swap and Earn tabs. The short version, on the site: [tacit.finance/build/#amm-doors](https://tacit.finance/build/#amm-doors). The rules: [`SPEC.md` §5.5](../SPEC.md#55-amm).
The contracts: [`DEPLOYMENTS.md`](./DEPLOYMENTS.md).

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > The pool
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > The pool]
A pool is a constant-product curve over two assets and a fee tier. Its id is `keccak256(lo, hi, feeBps)` with the
two asset ids sorted, so `(A, B)` and `(B, A)` are one pool. A pool with a protocol-fee switch is a separate pool with its own id. The reserves and the share total are public and sit in
one place, `ConfidentialPool.pools(poolId)`.

Any asset the pool holds can be paired: ETH (tETH), TAC, cBTC, cUSD, any ERC-20 registered with the pool, and
tokens issued on Bitcoin ([below](#one-pool-bitcoin-included)).

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Two doors
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Two doors]
| | Public | Private |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Call | `TacitPublicAmm.swapPublic`, from any wallet or contract | a settle that carries an `OP_SWAP` or `OP_SWAP_ROUTE` |
| Proof | none | one SP1 proof |
| Lands | in your transaction | when the proof is settled |
| In | tokens or ETH from your wallet | a note |
| Out | tokens or ETH to any address | a note |
| Visible | the sender and the amounts | the reserve change, not whose notes |
| Combines with | any other call in the same transaction | the ops in the same proof: a route of up to four pools |

Public in and private out also exists: `OP_WRAP_SWAP` turns a public deposit into the swap's output note, and
`OP_WRAP_LP` turns two public deposits into an LP-share note.

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Public swaps
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Public swaps]
```
swapPublic(assetIn, assetOut, feeBps, amountIn, minAmountOut, deadline, to)
```

- **No proof, so no proving wait.** The swap clears against the live reserves inside the transaction. The pool
  checks that the product of the reserves never falls, so the payout is bounded by the curve whatever the caller
  passes. `quoteSwap(assetIn, assetOut, feeBps, amountIn)` returns exactly what the swap pays.
- **Atomic with other calls.** `swapPublic` is an ordinary synchronous call, so anything that can call a contract
  can put it in one transaction with other calls, and the transaction either does all of it or none. The repository
  has several: the [swap card](../dapp/swap/) (the front page's Swap tab) takes any token through another pool to the asset, and the asset to any token, in one transaction;
  an order can be [split across the Precision pool and the Tacit pool](./TAC.md#trading-tac) in one transaction; and
  `ConfidentialRouter` has the swap, the liquidity add and the shielding of the position as single calls
  (`swapPublicPathWithPermit2`, `zapETHIntoLP`, `zapTokenIntoShieldedLP`, `zapETHIntoFarm`).
- **Bounds.** `minAmountOut` and `deadline` are the caller's. ETH goes in as `msg.value`; an ERC-20 needs an
  approval to `TacitPublicAmm`, or a permit through the router. Amounts are whole multiples of the asset's
  `unitScale` (TAC: `1e10`).

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Private swaps
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Private swaps]
A private swap spends a note of one asset and receives a note of the other. The proof checks that the input is a
member of the note tree, marks it spent, clears the swap at the pool's price, enforces the trader's minimum output
and keeps the product of the reserves from falling. Anyone can submit it: the relay proves it for a fee that is
bound inside the proof, or you prove and settle it yourself.

- **It clears at the live reserves.** The proof names the reserves it was built against, and the pool accepts it
  only while those are still the live ones. If another trade, public or private, moves them first, the settle is
  refused, nothing is spent, and the app builds a fresh quote. A public swap never waits on this: it reads the
  reserves in its own transaction.
- **What it hides.** Which note was spent and who holds the output. Reserves are public, so a lone swap moves them
  by its own amounts. Swaps that share an `OP_SWAP` batch clear at one price and move the reserves once, and
  `OP_SWAP_BLIND` keeps trade sizes from the SP1 prover and the chain as well, with the batcher that builds the batch
  seeing them ([`SPEC.md` §5.6](../SPEC.md#56-prover-blind-swaps)).

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Liquidity
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Liquidity]
| | Public position | Private position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Held as | a balance in `lpShares[poolId][address]` | an LP-share note |
| Add | `createPairAndAddLiquidityPublic`, one transaction | `OP_LP_ADD` (two notes in), `OP_WRAP_LP` (two deposits in) |
| Remove | `removeLiquidityPublic` | `OP_LP_REMOVE` |
| Visible | the holder and the size | neither |

Both kinds of share count in one `totalShares`: the public balances, the shares held in notes and the 1,000 shares
the first add locks forever. A public position can be turned into a private one in place with
`shieldShares(poolId, shares, commit)`, which burns the public shares into a pending deposit that an `OP_WRAP`
settle consumes into a note. The share total does not change, only the form of the claim.

**Yield.** A swap's fee stays in the reserves. Shares do not rebase; each share's claim on the reserves grows. On a pool
without a protocol-fee switch, every swap pays the same fee into the same reserves, so a private position earns
from public trading and a public one from private trading. Removal pays the pro-rata share of the reserves live at the settle, and a trade that lands
first cannot block it. LP-share notes can also be bonded into a farm, which earns TAC ([`FARMS.md`](./FARMS.md)).

**What stays visible.** The reserves, the share total and the change an add or a removal makes when it settles. The
position itself, whose it is and what it is worth, is a note.

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > One pool, Bitcoin included
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > One pool, Bitcoin included]
A Tacit note is the same commitment on both chains, and the pool holds the notes of every asset that reaches it:

| Asset | Where it comes from | In the pool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BTC | a self-custody lock on Bitcoin, with a bond behind it | cBTC, minted 1:1 |
| TAC and other Tacit tokens | issued on Bitcoin | a note, with an ERC-20 the pool mints |
| ETH | Ethereum | tETH, the same asset on both chains |
| ERC-20s | Ethereum | a wrapped note, one registration away |

Each chain proves its state to the other, so a bridge waits for a proof and never for a signature
([`BRIDGE.md`](./BRIDGE.md)). A note burned on Bitcoin is minted in the pool, and a note crossed out of the pool is
minted again on Bitcoin. A Bitcoin note bound to the pool can also be spent in the pool directly, with no bridge
step first ([`SPEC.md` §6.3](../SPEC.md#63-two-ways-bitcoin-value-reaches-ethereum)). A bridged note and a wrapped
one of the same asset are one asset, so they trade in the same pool.

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Read it yourself
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Read it yourself]
```
cast call $POOL "pools(bytes32)(bool,bytes32,bytes32,uint256,uint256,uint32,uint256)" $POOL_ID
cast call $PUBLIC_AMM "quoteSwap(bytes32,bytes32,uint32,uint256)(uint256)" $ASSET_IN $ASSET_OUT 30 $AMOUNT
```

`pools` returns `(init, assetA, assetB, reserveA, reserveB, feeBps, totalShares)` in in-system units, where a value
is the amount divided by `unitScale`. `assets(assetId)` gives the scale, and [`DEPLOYMENTS.md`](./DEPLOYMENTS.md) has
the addresses.

chunks.title: AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Source
chunks.text:
[AMM.md > The pool's AMM > Source]
| | |
| --- | --- |
| Pool, reserves and shares | [`ConfidentialPool.sol`](../contracts/src/ConfidentialPool.sol) |
| Public swap and liquidity | [`TacitPublicAmm.sol`](../contracts/src/TacitPublicAmm.sol) |
| Swaps and zaps in one call | [`ConfidentialRouter.sol`](../contracts/src/ConfidentialRouter.sol) |
| The last step of a swap from any token into tacUSD or tacBTC | [`TacitAmmRoute.sol`](../contracts/src/TacitAmmRoute.sol) |
| Private swap and liquidity ops | [`dapp/confidential-swap.js`](../dapp/confidential-swap.js), [`dapp/confidential-lp.js`](../dapp/confidential-lp.js) |

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit]
The Deposit tab on [tacit.finance/pay/eth](https://tacit.finance/pay/eth/) has a third mode, **Through a pool**: deposit ETH into the first
generation of [Privacy Pools](https://v1.privacypools.com/) (the ETH pool, about 770 ETH from 6,300 deposits at last read), watch its review, and
take it into a fresh Tacit receive address through a relayer. All of it happens on the page. The account is the pool app's own kind, so the same
deposits show in the pool's own app under the recovery phrase the panel shows, and the whole account comes back from the Tacit key alone.

The mode is off by default. Open the page once with `?pool=1` to turn it on in that browser (`?pool=0` turns it off).

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > What it is for
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > What it is for]
A withdrawal from the pool is an ordinary payment to an address, so the address that took it in has no on-chain link to the address that
deposited. The set a Tacit user hides in on the way in is the pool's, which is far larger than any one of Tacit's pools holds. It is the
**source** that is private. Tacit exits stay public (recipient and amount), and two sets never add up: the best case is the larger of the two.

The pool adds a rule of its own, the association set. Its approval service reviews each deposit and publishes the labels it approves; a
withdrawal proves the deposit is among them. A deposit that is not approved cannot be taken in, and its way out is the public exit back to the
depositing address.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > The account
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > The account]
Everything an account needs comes from the Tacit key.

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| Pool key | `sha256("tacit-assoc-pool-key-v1" ‖ tacit key)`, a plain secp256k1 key. It makes the deposits and signs the public exit. Any wallet that imports it reaches the same account. |
| Seed | The pool app's wallet-based key generation, run with the pool key: it signs the EIP-712 `DeriveSeed` message, HKDF-SHA256 over `r` (salt: the address) gives 32 bytes, shown as a 24-word phrase. |
| Master keys | BIP-39 → BIP-32 `m/44'/60'/{0,1}'/0/0` → two scalars → Poseidon → the master nullifier and secret. |
| Deposit `i` | nullifier and secret = `Poseidon(master, scope, i)`; child `j` of a deposit (change) = `Poseidon(master, label, j)`. |
| Discovery | Index 0, 1, … are hashed into precommitments and matched against the pool's `Deposited` events, stopping after 10 misses in a row. Each deposit's withdrawals follow its nullifiers. Where two deposits share a precommitment, the earlier is kept. |

**Recovery.** A new device with the same Tacit key finds every deposit, its review status and any change. To see them in the pool's own app,
show the recovery phrase in the panel and restore it there. A deposit made from another wallet with that phrase turns up under **Search every
deposit**. The exit of a deposit needs the address that made it: the pool key, or the wallet that was connected for it.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > The flow
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > The flow]
1. **Deposit.** From the pool key (the panel shows its address to fund) or the connected wallet. The minimum and the pool's cut are read from the
   entrypoint (0.01 ETH and 0.5% at last read).
2. **Reviewing, then Approved or Not approved.** The panel polls the approval service. A take-in proves membership in the list the service
   publishes, and the entrypoint accepts only the root it posted last, so a deposit approved a moment ago can wait a few minutes for the post. The
   page says so, and the deposit stays in the account.
3. **Take in.** Choose an approved deposit and an amount (any part; the change stays in the account). The page picks the next unused receive
   address that it already watches, asks the relayer for a quote, proves the withdrawal in a worker, and sends it to the relayer. The relayer's
   fee is 10 bps plus 650,000 gas at the current price, as a share of the amount; the page asks for the quote plus a fifth, within the entrypoint's
   maximum (10% at last read), and shows the amount that arrives. A very small amount is marked too small to relay at the current gas price.
4. **Exit.** A deposit that is not approved goes back to its depositing address with a proof from the small commitment circuit. This is public.

The proofs are made on the device, in a worker, with the pool's own circuits: the withdrawal circuit (about 20 MB) on the first take-in and the
commitment circuit (about 3 MB) on the first exit. The files are fetched from the pool's host, checked against the sha256 hashes in
[`dapp/assoc-pool.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool.js) (`CIRCUITS`, the hashes its own SDK pins), and kept in Cache Storage. A file with another hash is
refused.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > What other parties see
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > What other parties see]
| Party | Sees |
|---|---|
| The approval service | The page's IP and the labels it asks about. |
| The explorer API | The page's IP and queries by the pool key's address, which has no link to any Tacit address. |
| The relayer | The page's IP, the amount and the receive address it pays. |
| The chain | A deposit from the pool key or the wallet; later a relayed withdrawal to the receive address. |

As with any private payment, wait between the deposit and the take-in, take in a round amount, and use a receive address once. No server of
Tacit's is involved; the browser keeps the last few take-ins (amount and receive address) to avoid reusing an address.

A take-in earns no points: points follow public addresses, and a private source cannot earn them without being linked.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Code and hosts
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Code and hosts]
The modules are [`dapp/assoc-pool.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool.js) (pure: keys, trees, proofs' inputs, calldata, discovery),
[`assoc-pool-net.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool-net.js) (lists, events, terms, the relayer), [`assoc-pool-session.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool-session.js)
(the workflow), [`assoc-pool-prove-worker.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool-prove-worker.js) (proving) and [`assoc-pool-ui.js`](../dapp/assoc-pool-ui.js)
(the panel); [`bip39-english.js`](../dapp/bip39-english.js) is the word list, checked against its published hash. The page's content security
policy allows four hosts for it: the approval service (`api.0xbow.io`), the explorer API (`api.routescan.io`), the relayer (`fastrelay.xyz`) and
the pool's circuit files (`v1.privacypools.com`). No server of Tacit's is involved.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Tests
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Tests]
| Test | What it covers | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/assoc-pool.test.mjs` | The published BIP-32, BIP-39, EIP-712, RFC 5869 and circomlib vectors, the derivation, trees, context and calldata, discovery, withdrawal planning. | Nothing. |
| `tests/assoc-pool-net.test.mjs` | The service layer against stand-ins: lists, review status, log pages and a broken log, the entrypoint's terms, the relayer's fee and its refusals, completeness against the pool's counters. | Nothing. |
| `tests/assoc-pool-fork.mjs` | The live contracts and the pinned circuits on an anvil fork of mainnet: deposit, approval, a withdrawal to a Tacit receive box, rediscovery from the key, the change spent, the public exit, and the session workflow. | `anvil`, network, `ASSOC_ARTIFACTS=<dir with the six circuit files>`. |
| `tests/assoc-pool-page.mjs` | The page itself in Chromium on the same fork, with its content security policy on: the pool key, a deposit signed in the page, the withdrawal proved in the worker and relayed to the page's receive address, the account found again after a reload, the public exit, the recovery phrase. | The same, plus `PLAYWRIGHT=<path to playwright-core>`. |

The account was also read by the pool's own SDK: its `AccountService`, run on events made by this code, finds the same deposits, indices,
chains of change and exits, and the same next deposit index (463 primitive checks and 236 account checks). The one difference is a deposit's
change made with other keys: the SDK records an unspendable migration child, and this code stops at the note it still holds.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Trying it with a small amount
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Trying it with a small amount]
1. Sign in on [pay/eth](https://tacit.finance/pay/eth/?pool=1), Deposit → Through a pool, and send 0.01 to 0.02 ETH to the pool key's address
   (or connect a wallet and deposit from it).
2. Wait for **Approved** (from minutes to a day or more).
3. Show the recovery phrase and restore it in the pool's own app: the deposit and its status are there.
4. Take part of it in. The page shows the transaction, and the receive address sees the ETH.
5. Open the page on a clean browser profile with the same key: the deposit, the change and the take-in are found again.
6. A deposit that is not approved, or an approved one the owner wants back, is exited to the address that made it.

chunks.title: ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Scope
chunks.text:
[ASSOC-POOL.md > Through a pool: a private source for a deposit > Scope]
The panel reads the first generation's ETH pool. The second generation has its own contracts and set. Token pools use another asset address and
the same circuits, so the account, the discovery and the calls carry over, but the panel does not offer them.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge]
TAC, tETH and cBTC move between Bitcoin and Ethereum by proof. Each chain's state is proven to the other
in zero knowledge, and a bridge waits for a proof, never for a signature. No multisig, federation or
attestor set signs a bridge message. Nothing on Bitcoin had to change for it: it runs on Bitcoin and
Ethereum mainnet today.

The app: [tacit.finance/bridge](https://tacit.finance/bridge/). The rules: [`SPEC.md` §6](../SPEC.md#6-reflection-and-the-bridge).

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Reflection
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Reflection]
Each chain keeps a proven copy of the other's Tacit state. Bitcoin's blocks, once 24 deep, are folded
into proven roots; Ethereum's finalized blocks are verified by a light client; both go into one proof,
which the pool on Ethereum verifies. Nobody signs it, and anyone can make it.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Burn, prove, mint
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Burn, prove, mint]
Every bridge is three moves:

| | Bitcoin → Ethereum | Ethereum → Bitcoin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Burn** | The note is burned on Bitcoin. | The note is burned in the pool, and the cross-out is recorded in its storage. |
| **Prove** | Once 24 blocks deep, the burn is folded into Bitcoin's proof, and the pool verifies it. | Once Ethereum finalizes it, the cross-out is proven inside Bitcoin's proof. |
| **Mint** | The pool mints a fresh note of the same value, privately, once per burn. | A Bitcoin transaction mints a fresh note of the same value, once, as a proven member of the cross-outs. |

The amount is not published on either chain. Whoever makes the mint's proof sees it, and today that is
Tacit's prover.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > One format, two chains
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > One format, two chains]
A Tacit note is a Pedersen commitment `C = v·H + r·G` on secp256k1, the curve both chains already use. On
Bitcoin it is an output of a Taproot envelope, with a kernel signature and range proof; in the pool on
Ethereum it is a leaf of the note tree. A bridge burns a note on one chain and mints a fresh one of the same
value on the other, keeping `v` and picking a new `r`, with a proof that nothing was added or lost.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Bitcoin → Ethereum
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Bitcoin → Ethereum]
1. **Headers, by work.** `BitcoinLightRelay`, a permissionless relay on Ethereum, checks every Bitcoin
   header's proof of work and follows the heaviest chain. Anyone can submit headers.
2. **Every envelope folded.** The Bitcoin reflection program
   ([`reflect.rs`](../contracts/sp1/confidential/src/reflect.rs)) re-hashes each block to its Merkle root,
   checks the witness commitment, and folds every Tacit envelope in it: transfers, trades, AMM and farm
   ops, bridge burns, cBTC locks.
3. **One proof.** SP1 proves the fold. The pool accepts it only if its tip is an ancestor of the relay's
   tip buried at least 24 blocks deep, and it continues the digest the pool already holds.
4. **Checked by the pool.** `attestBitcoinStateProven` verifies the proof on-chain against
   `BITCOIN_RELAY_VKEY`. A proven burn is then minted into the pool once, keyed by its `burn_id`.

TAC the reflection follows is burned in one Bitcoin transaction. TAC it has not followed (a history that runs
through transfers from before reflection began) goes in two: a move to a burn address, then a burn whose
provenance, every transfer back to TAC's etch, is verified in the same proof (`fold_burn_deposit`). The proof
takes up to 256 transfers, the move among them.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Ethereum → Bitcoin
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Ethereum → Bitcoin]
1. **Finality, signed.** The Ethereum reflection program
   ([`eth-reflection`](../contracts/sp1/eth-reflection/src/main.rs)) is a light client built on sp1-helios.
   It checks the sync committee's signatures over finalized blocks, chained period to period from a pinned
   anchor, and binds to Ethereum mainnet's genesis validators root so no other chain's proof passes.
2. **The pool's storage.** Storage proofs against the finalized execution state root read the pool's
   cross-outs (`crossOutCommitment`), the Bitcoin notes it consumed, and its `EthCallOutbox` messages.
3. **Inside Bitcoin's proof.** The Bitcoin reflection program verifies the Ethereum proof recursively, so
   one proof, checked by the pool, carries both chains.
4. **Folded on Bitcoin.** A `T_CROSSOUT_MINT` re-mints a crossed-out note on Bitcoin only if its claim is
   proven a member of the cross-out set, and only once.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Who checks what
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Who checks what]
| Hop | Checked by |
| --- | --- |
| Bitcoin's history | Proof of work, on Ethereum, by a permissionless relay. A reorg deeper than the confirmation depth halts reflection rather than rewriting it. |
| Ethereum's finality | The sync committee's signatures, inside the proof. |
| Every state change | An immutable pool contract, against pinned verifying keys ([`DEPLOYMENTS.md`](./DEPLOYMENTS.md#verification-anchors)). |
| Bitcoin's side | The rules in `SPEC.md`: every indexer that runs them over the same chain reaches the same state, and the reflection proves that state. |
| The programs | Each rebuilds byte for byte from source and is pinned by SHA-256 to its key ([`REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.md`](./REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.md)). |

Reflection advances when someone runs the provers. The reference relayer does, and anyone else can.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself]
Tacit's services keep reflection current, and anyone can run it. Every step is an on-chain call that needs
no permission, and you pay only the network fee:

1. **Send the headers.** `BitcoinLightRelay.advanceTip(headers)` takes Bitcoin's block headers and checks
   each one's proof of work, so only real blocks are accepted.
2. **Make the proof.** Prove the batch the API holds open (below) with `bitcoin_prove` and your own
   account on Succinct's prover network. Everyone runs the same program on the same public inputs.
3. **Submit it.** `attestBitcoinStateProven(publicValues, proof)` accepts any valid proof over the pool's
   current state, from any wallet. Then `POST /reflection/landed`, and the API adopts the batch.

[tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/#tab=bitcoin) does the first and the last from your own wallet, and
[`tools/community-runner.mjs`](../tools/community-runner.mjs) does them on a loop from your own machine
([COMMUNITY-OPS.md](./COMMUNITY-OPS.md)). To
check the deployment itself, run [`tools/verify-live.mjs`](./VERIFY-LIVE.md) and rebuild the programs from
source ([`REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.md`](./REPRODUCIBLE-BUILDS.md)).

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself > The open batch
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself > The open batch]
The API (`https://api.tacit.finance`) holds open the batch it last assembled for Tacit's relay, byte for byte.
A landed copy of it is a batch the API already knows, so Tacit's relay goes on from it. These routes are public
and CORS-open.

| route | |
|---|---|
| `GET /reflection/open?network=mainnet` | `{ pool, job: { jobId, priorDigest, attestedTo, from, blocks, modeB, ethContentHash, bytes, at } \| null }`. Worth proving while the pool's `attestedReflectionDigest()` equals `priorDigest`. |
| `GET /reflection/open/job?network=mainnet&jobId=` | The batch (tens of MB); its `input` is the prover input. Three per caller, then one every five minutes. |
| `GET /reflection/eth-state/proof?network=mainnet&contentHash=` | For a batch with `modeB: 1`, the Ethereum proof it verifies inside (`ethCompressedProofB64`). |
| `POST /reflection/landed` | `{ network }` → `{ adopted, attestedTo }`. The API reads the pool's digest three blocks back from two endpoints and adopts only a batch it assembled. |
| `GET /reflection/burndep-list?network=mainnet` | The burns whose provenance bundles are registered for the reflection to fold. |

`bitcoin_prove` is the Linux x86-64 build in the `prover-bins` release that
[`worker-relay/Dockerfile`](../worker-relay/Dockerfile) names, pinned in `worker-relay/prover/bin/SHA256SUMS`.
Fund its account as in [`OPEN-RELAYER.md`](./OPEN-RELAYER.md#proving-with-your-own-prover-account).
`REFLECT_GAS_LIMIT` caps the request; the network holds that cap's cost from the credit while it proves.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself > The open batch
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Run it yourself > The open batch]
```sh
API=https://api.tacit.finance POOL=0x000000000Ed1eabD231Be41d93b719056F7febFC
J=$(curl -s "$API/reflection/open?network=mainnet" | jq .job)
cast call $POOL 'attestedReflectionDigest()(bytes32)' --rpc-url $RPC_URL    # must equal .priorDigest
curl -s "$API/reflection/open/job?network=mainnet&jobId=$(jq -r .jobId <<<"$J")" | jq .input > reflection_input.json
mkdir -p out
[ "$(jq .modeB <<<"$J")" = 1 ] && curl -s \
  "$API/reflection/eth-state/proof?network=mainnet&contentHash=$(jq -r .ethContentHash <<<"$J")" \
  | jq -r .ethCompressedProofB64 | base64 -d > out/eth_compressed.bin    # Mode-B only
PROOF_MODE=groth16 REFLECT_FIXTURE=reflection_input.json PROVER_OUT=out SP1_PROVER=network \
  NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY=0x… NETWORK_RPC_URL=https://rpc.mainnet.succinct.xyz REFLECT_GAS_LIMIT=20000000000 \
  worker-relay/prover/bin/bitcoin_prove
cast send $POOL 'attestBitcoinStateProven(bytes,bytes)' 0x$(cat out/bitcoin_pv.hex) \
  0x$(cat out/bitcoin_proof_bytes.hex) --rpc-url $RPC_URL --private-key 0x…
curl -s -X POST "$API/reflection/landed" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"network":"mainnet"}'
```

If another prover lands the same batch first, the pool's digest moves and your send fails its simulation.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > What you trust
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > What you trust]
Bitcoin's proof of work, Ethereum's validators (through its sync committee), and a proof system whose
pinned verifying keys anyone can rebuild from source. No signer set is in the path.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > How long it takes
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > How long it takes]
Bitcoin → Ethereum waits for 24 Bitcoin confirmations (about four hours) and then the next proof, which
lands on Ethereum about every half hour. Ethereum → Bitcoin waits for Ethereum to finalize (about 13
minutes), then for the next proof to cover the burn, then for the Bitcoin step to confirm: a few hours in
all. A two-step TAC bridge waits for the proof after the move and after the burn, usually within a day.
The burn is signed with the holder's key, so the app sends it while it is open with the wallet; a moved
note waits at its burn address until then, and can be moved back.
[tacit.finance/bridge](https://tacit.finance/bridge/) shows the live cadence and follows every bridge a
browser has under way.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets]
| Asset | To Ethereum | To Bitcoin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TAC | Burn on Bitcoin, minted privately in the pool once proven | Cross-out from the pool, minted on Bitcoin once proven |
| tETH | Burn on Bitcoin, minted back in the pool once proven | Cross-out from the pool |
| cBTC | Lock BTC at your own key's output, with a wstETH bond behind it; the pool mints cBTC 1:1 once the lock is proven. Borrow cUSD against it. | Will be burned on Bitcoin to redeem a lock |
| USDT | Burn on Bitcoin, minted back in the pool once proven | Cross-out from the pool, from private USDT (cUSDT) |

USDT is an Ethereum token the pool holds in escrow, so it keeps its six decimals and has no Bitcoin etch: it crosses under the id of its registration
in the pool, a hash of the chain and the token that no Bitcoin etch can produce, so the only USDT notes on Bitcoin are ones a cross-out made, each backed
by the USDT still in the pool's escrow. The pool's registry refuses to give an escrowed token a Bitcoin-side id of its own, and does not need to: a note
that comes back names the same id and resolves to the escrow directly. The USDT in a wallet is made private in the pool first (Permit2: one approval for
exactly the amount and one signature), and is taken out again to an Ethereum address once it is back.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Limits and costs, while the bridge is new
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Limits and costs, while the bridge is new]
| | To Bitcoin | Back from Bitcoin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TAC | 20 to 1,000 TAC a bridge | up to 1,000 TAC, a note goes whole |
| tETH | 0.001 to 0.5 tETH a bridge | up to 0.5 tETH, a note goes whole |
| USDT | 2 to 100 USDT a bridge | up to 100 USDT, a note goes whole |

A TAC note going back in two steps carries up to 255 transfers of history.

| What a bridge costs | To Bitcoin | Back from Bitcoin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relay fee | Taken out of the note: the relay's floor for the asset at today's gas (about 0.0005 tETH, 4 TAC). The note must be worth more than it. | None: Tacit covers the Ethereum mint for now |
| Bitcoin fee | About 900 to 1,200 sats at 1 to 2 sat/vB (a 180 vB reveal, a 154 vB commit, and the 546-sat output the note sits on), paid from the key's own Bitcoin address, which needs one free coin of about twice that when the Bitcoin step is sent, a few hours after the burn. A bridge can start without it: the app asks for the sats when the step is due, and the burn waits until they are there | About 1,000 sats at 1 to 2 sat/vB (two transactions, each at least 500), paid from the same address |

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Limits and costs, while the bridge is new
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Limits and costs, while the bridge is new]
[tacit.finance/bridge](https://tacit.finance/bridge/) shows what each way costs at the live rates. A USDT bridge must exceed its relay fee, which follows gas (about 3 USDT at 1.7 gwei, under 1 when gas is cheap; the way back is free, and a withdraw pays it again, about 2.5 USDT at 1.7 gwei). Its
Bitcoin steps are paid separately in sats (about 1,000 to 1,500 each, around a dollar). So the least that crosses moves with gas: 2 USDT is the form's floor, and at today's gas 5 is what gets through, arriving as about 2. The limits are in
[`crossout-ux.js`](../dapp/crossout-ux.js) and [`burndep-ux.js`](../dapp/burndep-ux.js); `tests/bridge-track.test.mjs`
holds the page's copy of them, and of the sizes behind the costs, to those files.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > In the app
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > In the app]
The Private ETH sheet's Bitcoin tab (`#private/bitcoin`) has the two ways side by side: **To Bitcoin**
(`#private/bitcoin/out`: the amount, the receipt, the bridges on their way) and **Back to Ethereum**
(`#private/bitcoin/back`: the notes the key holds on Bitcoin, the returns on their way, and a button to bring a
note back). It opens on the side the key has something to do on. The Private ETH balance carries a line for what the
key holds on Bitcoin and what is on its way there, and the same figures show on the dashboard and on the tETH page.
A note comes back whole, so bridge in the amounts you will want back.

[tacit.finance/bridge](https://tacit.finance/bridge/) does the same for the way to Bitcoin once the Tacit key is opened

there (nothing of the key or the wallet library is loaded until it is asked for): for TAC and tETH it takes the amount,

shows the receipt (what arrives, the relay's fee, the Bitcoin fee, the coin the Bitcoin step needs), asks for the

acknowledgement that a burn cannot be undone, and has the relay prove the burn, cutting a note to the exact amount

first when none fits. It also moves every bridge it lists on while the page is open, makes the presses a bridge row

waits on (burn, mint, move back, recover, check again, cancel, send again, sign again), and looks for bridges the

browser has no record of from the key's own Bitcoin address, or from the burn's Ethereum transaction and the amount.

For TAC it also starts a bridge from Bitcoin to Ethereum: it lists the TAC at the key's Bitcoin address with why a note

cannot go, checks the one picked and prices it against the coins the key has free for fees, asks for the same

acknowledgement, and sends the burn (one Bitcoin transaction) or, for a note the reflection does not yet track, the move

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > In the app
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > In the app]
that comes first; a note in an older form is first sent to the key's own address, and a note over 1,000 TAC is split.

With several notes it also offers Merge notes (the tracked notes packed within the limit, each pack sent to the key's own

address in one transaction) and Bridge all (the older notes sent first, a burn for each tracked note, a move then a burn for

a note the proof does not track yet), planned by the same rules as the front page, with the fee quoted first and, for Bridge

all, the same acknowledgement. A note sent first or merged is bridged from this page once it has confirmed and Bitcoin's proof

has seen it (the front page lists it under Getting ready too). Bridging a note for the holder when it is ready, minting to

someone else's address or as public TAC, proving a burn or a mint yourself, and paying the mint from a wallet are on the

front page; a press the relay will not take links there.

USDT has a sheet of its own (`#usdt`) with three tabs: **Make private** (USDT from the wallet into the pool), **Withdraw** (private USDT out to the wallet) and
**Bitcoin** (`#usdt/bitcoin/out`, `#usdt/bitcoin/back`: the bridge forms, as for cUSD and cBTC). The front page's Bridge tab takes USDT from the wallet, making it
private first when the key holds too little, and brings it back from Bitcoin.

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Following a bridge
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > The assets > Following a bridge]
Every bridge is journaled in the browser that started it, and the Bitcoin step needs the key, so a bridge can be left
and come back to: the app moves it on whenever it is open with the key, and so does the bridge page once the key is open
there (the engines hold a lease on each bridge they move, so two tabs never move one at once).
[tacit.finance/bridge](https://tacit.finance/bridge/) lists each bridge with what it waits on, and names a step as ready as soon as the chains say so (the proof has
reached its burn), whether or not the app has been open since. A tab left open there puts the count of bridges that
need their holder in its title, and can send a browser notification when one does, or when one arrives (off until
asked for).

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > On mainnet
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > On mainnet]
The ERC-20 supply of TAC (~2.5M) was all minted by the pool from TAC proven to have left Bitcoin. TAC has
made the whole round trip, each leg a settled transaction:

1. Out of the pool: [`0xc7bfc7ce…3c29a8f`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0xc7bfc7cec938e59c5d256d1c44c2aea5269eb7c237ac018878f21b2a93c29a8f)
2. Minted on Bitcoin: [`aaa68792…97bcf2`](https://mempool.space/tx/aaa687924435ef64f056aa83beb7fabef4f57087f315655b52c596f83897bcf2)
3. Burned on Bitcoin: [`7320b6b6…36b0fbb`](https://mempool.space/tx/7320b6b654726ba99489bcf47f3d31dcf8a87040241def827b5fccd8836b0fbb)
4. Back in the pool, as a fresh note: [`0f0793f6…006465bb`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x0f0793f61e57a0eb40ef551ef516e9a33ba0f270343abedf4ea014aa006465bb)

chunks.title: BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Next: covenants
chunks.text:
[BRIDGE.md > The Tacit bridge > Next: covenants]
When Bitcoin can enforce where an output is spent (CTV, `OP_CAT`, `OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK` or an
equivalent), a cBTC lock becomes a vault that only a redemption opens, minted with no bond behind it.
The bytes are already reserved ([`SPEC.md` §10](../SPEC.md#10-extensions-and-covenant-placeholders)).

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge]
A liquidity provider (LP) swaps the same asset across Bitcoin and Ethereum with an adaptor-signature atomic swap, so a
holder of TAC on Bitcoin has TAC in the Ethereum pool in about the time of one Bitcoin block and one Ethereum settle,
instead of waiting for the reflection. The reflection bridge is unchanged: the LP rebalances over it, off the user's
clock.

Neither party holds the other's funds at any point. Each leg is enforced by its own chain: a Taproot script on
Bitcoin, the pool's lock set on Ethereum. The only thing that links them is a secret `t`.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum]
1. The LP publishes its Bitcoin claim key and a quote (amount in, amount out, windows, and `takeSats`, the fee of its take:
   `546 + 750 vB × 2 × the fee rate`, which the user's client accepts up to 30,000 sats).
2. The user picks a note, derives `t` and `T = t·G` from its key and the note's outpoint, and moves the amount into a
   Taproot output keyed `P_LP + T` with a refund leaf `<csv> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY OP_DROP <user> OP_CHECKSIG`. A
   sealed OP_RETURN in the same transaction lets the user find the lock again from its key, and a plain output of
   `takeSats` to the LP's own address pays for the take, so a provider needs no Bitcoin of its own: by the time it takes,
   that output is confirmed with the lock. The LP refuses a lock that does not pay it, and keeps it if the user refunds.
3. The user sends the LP its lock offer. The LP reads the lock from the chain: the transaction and the notes it
   spends, the note the validator derives, its asset and commitment, its confirmations, and whether a spent note is
   already consumed on Ethereum.
4. After the confirmations its policy asks for, the LP moves a pool note of exactly the amount into the pool's lock
   set under `(T, deadline, recipient = the user's claim key)` and sends the user the lock terms and a
   pre-signature of the claim kernel, adapted to `T`.
5. The user finds the lock in the pool, checks the pre-signature, and claims: the kernel completes with `t`, and the
   claim's public values carry the completed signature `z`.
6. The LP reads `z` from the settle, computes `t = z − s̃` and spends the Bitcoin lock by key path with `d_LP + t`.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum]
If a party stops, each side refunds on its own: the LP's lock after the Ethereum deadline, the user's lock after the
Bitcoin timelock. Ethereum to Bitcoin is the same swap with the roles exchanged: the LP holds `t` and locks Bitcoin
first, the user locks the pool note.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > What each side reads from the chain
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > What each side reads from the chain]
Nothing in an offer stands in for a chain read. The Ethereum locker takes the swap id from the outpoint the lock
transaction spends, the note and its asset from the validator, the confirmations from the chain, the lock output's
script from the transaction, and whether the spent notes are consumed on Ethereum from the pool. The Bitcoin locker
accepts an Ethereum offer only when the lock leaf is in the pool's lock set, the leaf recomputes from the stated
terms, and the pre-signature verifies against the output it chose. A pre-signature over `(L − O)` exists only if the
locked note holds exactly the quoted amount.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
Nothing in the pool or the swap is specific to one provider: a provider is a Tacit key with private TAC that answers a user's requests and takes the Bitcoin. Providers find users, and users find them, without a server of
the provider's own:

- **An ad.** A provider signs an ad with its claim key: its terms (fee, limits, timelock), what it can take now, and the gateway
  key requests are sealed to. An ad stands for a few minutes and is posted again every minute. A user's page checks each
  ad's signature itself, whoever delivered it.
- **A board.** The ads are posted to a small board, which also carries requests and answers: a request is sealed to the
  provider's gateway key and an answer to the request's one-time key (the private route's sealing, `dapp/sealed-request.js`),
  and only the provider the request was for can post its answer. The board can drop or delay a message and can read, change
  or answer none. The requests are the ones of the HTTP API, so a provider in a browser tab, which cannot serve a request,
  answers what a daemon does. A provider that serves HTTP can be listed directly as well.
- **A choice.** The page asks every provider that can take the amount for a quote, shows the best, and asks the next best
  when the first cannot hold the payout.
- **A wait.** When no provider online takes the amount, the page keeps a want for the key in the browser and posts it to the
  boards, signed by a key made for it alone, for up to a day. Providers see what is waiting (the provider panel, and an alert in
  the daemon); the holder is told on `/fast/`, and on the front page once, when a provider can take it. A want moves nothing.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
A provider in a page is for modest amounts: it answers requests and takes the Bitcoin while the page is open, and swaps that
are open when the page closes are tended again the next time the key is opened. A provider that is a process (`fastbridge-lp/`)
keeps them tended without a page.

**Which notes a provider can take.** A lock's notes need only be valid Tacit notes, the validator's verdict, and that includes a
note made by an exit from the Bitcoin shielded pool (`T_BTC_SPEND`, opcode 0x6d). Such a note cannot be bridged home by burning
it: the burn's proof follows transfers back to the etch and does not follow a history through the pool. TAC a provider takes this
way stays on Bitcoin, where it can be traded. A provider that rebalances by bridging home screens locks with the regular
bridge's own trace (`POST /reflection/burndep/trace` answers a note like this with "opcode 0x6d") and refuses such a lock after it is
on Bitcoin, when its fees are spent and its TAC waits out the timelock. The reference provider takes any TAC the validator accepts, and says so:
its `/info` and its signed ad carry `anyTac: true`. A provider that says nothing of it is taken to screen. A provider run from the
`/fast/` page has a switch for it ("Take TAC that came out of the shielded pool", on by default): switched off, it leaves `anyTac` out
of its terms and refuses a lock that spends a note the bridge's proof cannot follow, before it takes the lock (`policy.screen` in
`dapp/fastbridge-el.js`, built from the same check the page uses). The LP daemon has no such switch: it takes any TAC and says so.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
The holder never picks a kind of TAC. The page sends each lock to the best provider that takes what it must spend (`begin` in
`dapp/fast/wire.js`). Notes the proof follows go to any provider; a provider that screens is given only such notes, looked at before
the lock is built with the trace (`lineage` in `dapp/burndep-ux.js`; a note the reflection tracks needs no trace, and a trace that
cannot be read stops the lock rather than guess). Notes it cannot follow (a pool or farm trade, an exit from the shielded pool, TAC
that came over from Ethereum) go only to a provider that takes any TAC, and the page passes over a better quote from a provider that
screens for one that does. When no provider online takes what must be spent, the page says so and locks nothing. A history longer
than the proof folds (255 transfers) is not looked at this way: the trace's verdict on it is a limit and not a refusal, and whether a
provider takes it is the provider's rule. The Bridge tab offers the fast bridge for a note the regular bridge cannot follow when a
provider online takes any TAC.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > On the front page
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > On the front page]
The Bridge tab's way in for TAC from Bitcoin prefers the fast bridge: when a note is picked, the tab asks the providers there are
(`dapp/fast/lp.json`, the boards) whether one takes that amount now. If one does, the tab quotes the bridge through the best of them
(`dapp/fast/route.js`): what arrives, the provider's fee, the Bitcoin cost (the lock is built and signed as a dry run, so an address that
cannot pay for it is told before the press), about how long it takes, and what happens if the provider stops. The first press says that and
locks nothing; the same press again begins the bridge with exactly the note picked. The regular bridge (a burn and the reflection, a few
hours, no provider fee) stays one press away under the receipt, and is the way when no provider takes the size, with the reason in its
receipt. The steps of a bridge through a provider are taken while any page of the site is open with the key (one tab at a time holds the
lock), and a bridge that ends is said once. `?fast=0` turns the preference off in a browser (`?fast=1` on again).

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- The counterparty's Bitcoin claim key is fixed before `t` exists, and the lock is built to that key.

- Each swap has exactly one Ethereum lock, and no two locks share an `L`: the claim kernel is over `(L, O)`. The

  Ethereum locker derives the blinding of `L` from its seed, the swap id and the whole adaptor point. It computes the

  Ethereum deadline once, from the block time at which the Bitcoin lock reached its confirmations, and stores it with the

  swap. A lock that is stored is sent from its stored bytes; a lock that may already be in the pool is looked up by its

  leaf before anything new is built; a lock that is found too late to answer is still watched and refunded. The record

  of an open swap is the safety state of the Ethereum locker and is kept durably and backed up. An offer that reaches

  the Ethereum locker long after its lock confirmed is not answered, which bounds what a lost record can lead to.

- The Ethereum locker takes only what it can lock. A quote checks its inventory and holds nothing; a reservation holds the

  payout when the user commits, before it locks any Bitcoin, and is extended once the lock is on the network and held

  through its confirmation. An offer whose payout is not held is held at that moment or declined. A provider that is out of

  inventory is therefore found out while the user's TAC is still in hand.

- Steps of one swap run one at a time, so overlapping ticks never build the same transaction twice.

- The Ethereum locker answers an offer only for a lock with a confirmation (a lock in the mempool can be replaced), checks the outpoint's

  shape and the amounts against the quote before it asks any explorer, and ends a swap whose lock does not reach its confirmations in time.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- A lock that is built again (the relay lost the job, or said it failed) is built from the note the first try used, so that if the first lands

  after all the second cannot: two locks of one swap would insert one leaf twice and strand a note. A note no longer held is waited for, not

  replaced, since the pool then shows the first lock by its leaf.

- What a settle did is read only from a settle the pool or its relayer was called with. Bytes that look like a settle inside the calldata of

  another contract's call are whatever their sender wrote.

- A stored take or refund whose funding coin was spent elsewhere is built again once it has had time to spread.

- A provider holds a payout for a swap, not for a quote: an offer is held at its arrival, under the lock that checks capacity, so two offers

  arriving together cannot both be given what is left for one. A reservation is extended once, by a transaction that pays the take, and one

  transaction stands for one quote.

- A lock is made from a pool note of exactly the amount. When there is none, one is cut from a larger note, once, and

  the tries that follow are spaced by growing waits, since each reads the wallet's notes.

- No claim is built with less than `minClaimSecs` left before the deadline: a claim that is sent and misses the

  deadline still publishes `t`.

- Time on Ethereum is the latest block's timestamp. The Ethereum locker refunds only after the deadline plus a margin,

  and looks for a claim again before every refund step, so a claim that lands near the deadline still opens the

  Bitcoin lock.

- Once the Bitcoin timelock has run, the Bitcoin locker takes its note back from any waiting phase, so a claim job

  that never answers or an offer that cannot be read does not hold it.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- The Ethereum locker signs its take over the sats value the lock output really carries, read from the transaction.

- Every field of an offer is checked for shape before it is used; a field that does not parse is refused with a reason.

- The pre-signature nonce binds the excess, `(L, O)`, the full compressed `T` and the lock leaf.

- Every record is stored before the step that sends it, and the step is resumed from the stored bytes.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Windows
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Windows]
| | default |
|---|---|
| Bitcoin refund timelock | 144 blocks |
| Ethereum lock window | 4 h from the block that confirmed the Bitcoin lock, rounded up to 10 min |
| Minimum time left to claim | 1 h |
| Slack between the Ethereum deadline and the opening of the Bitcoin refund | 2 h |
| Confirmations before the LP locks | policy by amount (1 for small, more for large) |

`checkEvmDeadline` and `btcRefundOpensAt` in `dapp/adaptor-xswap.js` hold the arithmetic: the Bitcoin refund must open
at least the slack after the Ethereum deadline, and the Ethereum locker needs time to see `z` and get its Bitcoin
claim mined before then.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Proving the claim
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Proving the claim]
The claim's proof is made by someone who sees `z` before the claim lands. The claimer therefore chooses its prover:
its own machine, its own credit on a prover network, or a relay that is not the LP. Adaptor jobs are not offered to the
open proof board for the same reason. `adaptorlock` and `adaptorclaim` are expiring job types in the relay, so a relay
that is paused or held skips a job whose deadline has passed instead of sending it.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready]
A holder can also skip the provider. One Bitcoin transaction binds TAC to the pool (`T_CXFER_BOUND`, 0x39): the notes it makes
sit at the key's Taproot address, keyed to it, with blindings from the key's own change channel, so the key alone finds and
opens them again. Once the reflection has folded that transaction (24 blocks, then its proof), each bound note moves into the
pool by the fast lane (SPEC §6.3) in one settle: a transfer whose input is proven in the reflected Bitcoin root and absent from
the reflected spent set, signed by the note's Taproot key. The relay settles it for a fee taken from the note, so no ETH is
needed. The wait is paid once, when the TAC is made ready, not when it moves.

- `dapp/btc-bind.js`: the bind (`bindTransfer`, at most 8 notes of chosen sizes), `openBoundNote`, and `fastLaneNote`, which asks

  `POST /reflection/note-witness` (leaves and nullifiers) and checks its roots against the pool's (`knownBitcoinRoot`, slot 78,

  and `knownBitcoinSpentRoot`, slot 79) before anything is proven; a settle against any other spent root reverts.

- `dapp/fast/wire.js` `openBound` and `dapp/fast/bound.js`: the "Ready for Ethereum" panel on `/fast/`, unlisted while it is

  new (only `/fast/#ready` shows it), 10 to 1,000 TAC a bind. A bind spends the key's tracked TAC at its trading address and,

  where they are, the TAC that came back from Ethereum (cross-out mints at its Taproot address, spent by key path).

- Rules that keep it whole: a bound note is never a lot (a purchase refuses it), since its holder could still move it to Ethereum

  and void the buyer's side until the reflection passes the spend; a note bound to a pool the wallet cannot read is pending; the

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready]
Bitcoin shielded pool's replay refuses any input whose history holds a bound note. A transfer out of a bound note is pending

  until the reflection passes its block, so a provider's lock check already refuses a lock that spends one too early.

- A bridge to Bitcoin can arrive ready (`crossout-ux.js` `start({ ready })`, the front page's "Arrive ready to come back fast",

  offered and ticked by default in a browser that has opened `/fast/#ready`, unless the holder last unticked it). It arrives when

  its mint is credited, like any bridge; then, under the open key, the page's bridge tick binds what it minted where it landed

  (`bindNow`, key path at the Taproot address, a failure kept as `bindError` and rested), so the TAC is ready about four hours

  later with no step of the holder's. The pool and guests are unchanged: a cross-out still mints an ordinary note.

- "Use on Bitcoin" turns a bound note back into ordinary TAC at the trading address (`unbindTransfer`, a plain transfer by key

  path, opened by the wallet's own change channel), usable on Bitcoin once the reflection passes it.

- Limits that stay, the pool and guests being kept as they are: the fast lane's signature has no deadline, a bound note names one

  pool deployment, and a fast-lane spend made while a reflection proof is out makes that proof stale (it is proven again). Binds

  are kept small (10 to 1,000 TAC) for that reason.

chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Code]
| `dapp/fastbridge-client.js` | the user's side as a whole: terms and quote checked before they are shown, the notes to lock, the machine over a store, the words for each phase, a lock found again from the key |

Each machine takes its chain access as arguments (`ctx`, documented in its header), keeps one JSON record per swap,
and advances with `step(record)`.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits]
- A provider prices as it likes. A bridger's client quotes a fee up to 90% of the amount and flags one over 5% (`highFee`): the fast page
  says so in the receipt and at the first press, and the front page's Bridge tab keeps the regular bridge as its choice and says the fast
  page can still do it (`dapp/fast/fmt.js`, `route.js`). A fee over 90% is not quoted.

- A board is a memory-only relay: it can be filled with junk requests (64 for each provider for ten minutes) and its ad slots with

  throwaway keys. An ad is signed by the claim key only, so a provider whose ad has lapsed can have its gateway key named in an ad of

  someone else's until that one lapses. Both need a change to the ad's format (a gateway signature) and a deploy of the board and the pages

  together; the board's runs now carry an id, so a provider reads again from the start after a board restart.

- The quotes of a provider are kept until two days after they ran out; the file store reads every record for each capacity check.

- The pre-signature is served to anyone who asks after the pool lock is made; a lock that is reorganised away after the provider's

  confirmations (one for the smaller amounts) can be double-spent by its maker. The confirmations policy is the defence.

- The claim's proof is made by the claimer's chosen prover; see "Proving the claim".

- Wants cost nothing to make up: the board takes 30 an hour from one address (`fastbridge-lp/board.mjs`, which needs

  `FB_BOARD_TRUST_PROXY` behind Render's proxy to tell addresses apart), and a provider's panel lists each by size with how many it can take.

- When the relay is held (its settle wallet under its gas floor) it proves but does not send. The pages then send each settle from the

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits]
connected Ethereum wallet after 45 s (`fastbridge-evm.js` jobStatus, `fast/wire.js` walletSettle): an open-board job with its proof, and

  an adaptor lock, claim or refund (which never go on the open board) proved again prove-only. The sender's address is public on

  Ethereum, so a bridger who sends its own claim links that address to the claim; the wallet asks first. `tests/fastbridge-fork.mjs` C

  runs a whole swap this way through the settle guest on a fork.

- The device prover does not take the adaptor ops yet (`device-prover.js` DEVICE_TYPES). Nothing in them goes stale while a laptop

  proves (the pool accepts any lock-set root it has known), so adding them is a matter of wiring and a guest run on the device.

`HARNESS` is a directory holding `exec-adaptor{lock,claim,refund}` built from `contracts/sp1/confidential/harnesses`
with `cargo build --release --bin exec-adaptorlock --bin exec-adaptorclaim --bin exec-adaptorrefund`. They embed the
