chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status]
Built and tested: the protocol, the transaction builders, both role machines, a simulated chain, the full swap in both
directions against the real settle guest and the real note validator, the pool adapter, the LP process with its
HTTP API, store and explorer adapter, the board and the mailbox over it, and the bridge page (`/fast/`) with its client,
recovery from the key, a choice among providers, a provider mode for any key, and a browser check. The page reads its
board from `dapp/fast/lp.json`.

Not built: the Ethereum to Bitcoin direction, the claim prover's options
(the relay that is not the provider, the user's device, a prover network), and a run with real funds.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops]
Bitcoin's state reaches Ethereum through calls anyone can make: block headers into the header relay, proofs of
each batch into the pool, and the open board's settles into the pool for the fees their proofs pay. Tacit's own
services make every one of them. So can you, from a browser wallet on
[tacit.finance/prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) (its Relay and Bitcoin tabs), or from your own machine with one key and the
**community runner**, [`tools/community-runner.mjs`](../tools/community-runner.mjs).

The page and the runner build the same calls from the same modules:
[`dapp/header-relay-advance.js`](../dapp/header-relay-advance.js) for headers and
[`dapp/community-ops.js`](../dapp/community-ops.js) for proofs and the board.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
Node 22 or later. Node 20 runs everything but the Nostr board unless started with `--experimental-websocket`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/src-company/tacit
cd tacit && npm ci --omit=dev
DRY_RUN=1 ONCE=1 node tools/community-runner.mjs           # what it would send now; no key needed
RUNNER_KEY=0x… node tools/community-runner.mjs             # all three modes, each on its own loop
RUNNER_KEY=0x… node tools/community-runner.mjs settles     # one mode: headers, attest or settles
node tools/community-runner.mjs mirror                       # keep the board public on Nostr; no key, no gas
```

Use a fresh key that holds only ETH for gas. The board pays its fees to the sending account, and an account with
code (an EIP-7702 delegation) runs that code on them; the runner says so at start when the key has code.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
| env | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `RUNNER_KEY` | | The account that signs, pays the gas and is paid the board's fees. Not needed with `DRY_RUN=1`. |
| `RPC_URL` | `https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com` | Reads and simulation. |
| `SEND_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc.flashbots.net/fast?hint=hash` | Where signed transactions go. Flashbots Protect does not include a transaction that would revert, and keeps it out of the public mempool. |
| `API_BASE` | `https://api.tacit.finance` | Published proofs, the board, landings. |
| `ESPLORA_URL` | `https://blockstream.info/api` | Bitcoin's headers. |
| `DRY_RUN=1` | | Simulate and print what would be sent; send nothing. |
| `ONCE=1` | | One pass of each mode, then exit (status 1 if a pass failed). |
| `HEADERS_SECS` `ATTEST_SECS` `SETTLES_SECS` | 300, 60, 15 | Each mode's cadence. A pass that sent something, or passed over a job the pool refused, runs again at once. |
| `HEADERS_MIN_BEHIND` | 3 | See *headers*. |
| `HEADERS_NEED` | | A Bitcoin height to carry the relay to, whatever the pacing: a cBTC lock's or bridge deposit's block + 24. |
| `ATTEST_AFTER_SECS` | 120 | See *attest*. |
| `MARGIN_BPS` | 2000 | See *settles*. |
| `NOSTR` | 1 | Read and copy the board on public Nostr relays (see *settles*). 0: the API's board alone. |
| `NOSTR_RELAYS` | `wss://relay.damus.io`, `wss://nos.lol`, `wss://relay.primal.net`, `wss://offchain.pub` | Comma separated. |
| `MAX_GAS_GWEI` | 5 | Headers, attests and ancestry calls wait while the base fee is above this. 0 turns the ceiling off. |
| `PRIORITY_GWEI` | 0.1 | The tip each transaction offers. |

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
Every transaction is run against the latest block from the runner's own address before it is signed, and its gas
limit comes from the node's estimate. Transactions go one at a time; each is waited for (up to 3 minutes) before
the next. Work someone else finished meanwhile is passed over: a header batch already on the relay, a proof the
pool has moved past, a settle another sender landed.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > headers
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > headers]
Sends Bitcoin's block headers, read from the explorer, to `BitcoinLightRelay.advanceTip`, at most 40 a
transaction. The relay checks each header's proof of work, and the runner refuses to extend a relay whose tip is
not the explorer's block at that height (a fork needs an operator).

- **When.** The next proof is waiting on the relay (the relay has not confirmed past the proven block) and the relay
  is at least `HEADERS_MIN_BEHIND` blocks behind Bitcoin's tip less 2. Tacit's own relay usually keeps within a
  block or two, so the runner sends when it falls behind. It advances as far as the reflection can use soon:
  Bitcoin's tip less 2, or the proven block + 24 + 110, whichever is lower.
- **Costs.** About 92,000 gas a transaction plus 172,000 a header (15 headers estimated 2.68 million gas).
- **Earns.** Nothing on chain. It keeps bridge deposits and cBTC locks moving.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > attest
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > attest]
Lands a proof of Bitcoin's state that Tacit's prover has published (`GET /reflection/proof`) and not landed, with
`ConfidentialPool.attestBitcoinStateProven(publicValues, proof)`.

- **When.** The proof still builds on the pool's attested digest, and it was published at least
  `ATTEST_AFTER_SECS` ago. Tacit's prover lands its own proofs, usually within that time.
- **Ancestry.** While the proofs are more than 2,016 blocks behind the relay's confirmed tip, no batch can reach
  them, so this mode calls `advanceReflectionAncestry()` first: each call walks up to 2,016 of the relay's blocks
  toward a checkpoint the next batch can build on, and the runner calls it until the gap closes.
- **Costs.** An attest uses about 0.4 to 0.6 million gas (a recent one used 419,593). An ancestry call walks up to
  2,016 relay blocks and costs more; its estimate is logged before it is sent.
- **Earns.** Nothing on chain. Bridge deposits up to the proven block can mint once it lands.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles]
Sends the open board's settles with `ConfidentialPool.settle(publicValues, proof, memos)`. The board is read from
two places, and either one alone is enough:

- Tacit's API (`GET /confidential/open`, see [OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md)). A landing is reported back
  (`POST /confidential/landed`).
- Public Nostr relays: proofs that holders, /prove/ tabs and other runners posted there
  ([`dapp/nostr-board.js`](../dapp/nostr-board.js)). Each pass also copies the API's open jobs that no relay carries
  yet, so the board stays public if the API stops answering. A job read from Nostr alone needs no report: the chain
  is its record.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles]
- **When.** A job is open (no other sender has taken it), whole, and more than two minutes from its deadline, by
  the latest block's time. Of those, the runner takes the oldest whose fee pays its gas with `MARGIN_BPS` to
  spare: first at 600,000 gas, then again at the job's own estimate. A job the pool refuses in simulation is passed
  over for ten minutes.
- **What a fee is worth.** tETH legs at their face value in ETH. TAC legs at 80% of the TAC/tETH pool's spot price,
  read from the pool's reserves at most once a minute. The discount covers the price risk of being paid in TAC.
  Moving that price far enough to fool a sender costs more than the gas a sender could lose.
- **Costs.** A recent transfer's settle used 348,054 gas; the runner prices a job at 600,000 before its own estimate.
- **Earns.** Each fee leg the proof binds, paid to the sending account inside the same transaction: tETH legs as
  ETH, TAC legs as TAC. A fork of mainnet replaying a real settle paid the runner its 0.0062 ETH fee less 0.000084 ETH
  of gas. Legs in other assets are paid too but are not counted when choosing what to send. Jobs reach the board when
  Tacit's relay has proved a settle it is not sending yet, or when a holder posts a proof made with their own prover
  (tacit.finance offers this when its relay is not proving: the holder's computer proves the action with a fee for
  its sender). Tacit's relay sends its own as soon as it can, so the first sender is paid.
- The board API allows a burst of 30 reads and one every 2 seconds after that, per IP address.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > mirror (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > mirror (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
Copies the API's open jobs to the Nostr relays, as *settles* does on each pass, and sends nothing. It needs no key
and no gas, so anyone can keep the board public. Up to four jobs a minute, each posted once an hour.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
Race Tacit's own prover for the prover board's public jobs. These are ops whose program input holds no one's secret: a wrap, and a swap or a payment from a staged deposit (a deposit only its key can spend, made ahead of the press). `board` claims one at a time (`POST /prover/community/claim` with your address), proves it with `tacit-prover` beside it and hands the proof back. Claiming takes the job from no one: Tacit's worker goes on with it, the relay checks each proof that comes back as it checks its own (a simulated settle) and uses the first that passes. A proof that does not pass costs nothing but a mark on the board's summary against the address.

- **Needs:** `tacit-prover` running, and `MINER=0x…`, the address the board credits. No key and no ETH: nothing is sent on chain.
- **Who wins:** a press waits a few minutes at most, so a machine that proves in under a minute (a desktop GPU) wins races; a laptop's 10 to 15 minutes does not. After its first proof the runner passes over a job due sooner than its last proof took. Laptops earn more from [Prove for the wrap pool](#prove-for-the-wrap-pool), whose wraps wait.
- **Points:** each proof the relay takes earns the address `POINTS_BOARD_PER_PROOF` points (20 by default) for at most `POINTS_BOARD_DAILY_CAP` proofs a UTC day (30); a refused or unchecked proof earns nothing, and 0 for either switches it off. The day's tally is at `GET /prover/board/credits?day=<n>`, the proof pool's shape. The mining campaign pays it once its URL is added to the points service's `POINTS_MINE_FEED` after the pool's, comma-separated: each address's points from both are summed for the day, and each feed caps the day on its own.
- **Off:** `PROVER_BOARD_COMMUNITY=0` on the API closes the routes.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > Not included: overflow drains
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > Not included: overflow drains]
`drainOverflow` and `drainOverflowRoots` apply effects a batch deferred past its per-attest cap. Their inputs are
the deferred items themselves (lock spends and redemptions, locks, asset metadata, calls) in the guest's committed
order, but an attest publishes only each chunk's running-keccak root. The items exist only inside the reflection
guest's run over that batch's Bitcoin blocks, which neither the chain nor the API publishes, so a runner cannot
build the call from public data. `pendingOverflowChunks()` on the pool reads 0 today.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
A page with a Tacit account open asks the proof pool to keep wraps of a few sizes proved ahead, so the deposit that follows needs no wait for a proof. Any
computer can make those proofs. `tacit-prover` leases one wrap at a time from the pool (`GET /prover/pool`), proves it and sends the proof back; the API
keeps it only if its public values are the wrap's and the live SP1 verifier takes it, and credits the address you named with points. Tacit's own GPU
prover leaves a wrap to community provers first (up to ten minutes by default, and only while one has asked in the last five), so a computer that asks gets first pick.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- 0xYourAddress    # install it and start it at login
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- --status         # running? what waits in the pool? what has the address earned?
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall      # stop it and remove it
```

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
[tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) gives the same command with your address filled in, then starts and pauses the installed prover and shows the
proof under way and what the address has earned (it talks to `tacit-prover` on 127.0.0.1: `GET /mine`, `POST /mine {miner, on}`, kept in
`~/.tacit-prover/mine.json`). [`dapp/prove.sh`](../dapp/prove.sh) picks the build
for the machine (an Apple-silicon Mac or x86-64 Linux; on Windows, run it inside WSL 2, see [On Windows](../contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/README.md#on-windows)), downloads the release it pins and runs nothing from it unless the
archive's sha256 is the pinned one, puts the program in `~/.tacit-prover/bin`, and sets it to start at login (a launchd agent, or a systemd user unit). Run
again, it updates the program and keeps the address. Cutting a new release means `node tools/prove-pins.mjs tacit-prover-vX.Y.Z`, which writes its sums into the script.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
- **Needs:** about 8 GB of memory. The first proof downloads SP1's Groth16 circuit once, 6.2 GB (8.4 GB unpacked). A proof takes about 5 to 10 minutes on a Mac
  with 16 GB or more (13 minutes measured on an 8 GB MacBook Air) and uses the processor while it runs, so a laptop does best plugged in. The program makes one proof
  at a time and asks the pool for the next as soon as one is done (once a minute while the pool is empty).
- **Costs:** nothing else. No key and no ETH are involved and nothing is signed; the address only receives points. A proof it cannot make is handed back, unpaid.
- **Earns:** 20 points a proof, the first 30 of a day. Once the day is over, the points service shares that day's TAC between the provers by points, no point
  paid more than a cap, so a proof pays up to 20 times the cap. [`GET https://tacit-points.onrender.com/mine`](https://tacit-points.onrender.com/mine) gives the
  terms, when they end and what is left in the pocket; add `?address=0x…` for what an address has been credited. The keeper page and `--status` read it.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device]
The runner makes no proofs; it lands proofs others publish. Proving an op with your own hardware is
[`contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/`](../contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/); proving with your own
Succinct account is in [OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md#proving-with-your-own-prover-account).

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Tests
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Tests]
```sh
node --test tests/community-ops.test.mjs tests/community-runner.test.mjs   # the shared module and the runner, stubbed
node tests/community-runner-fork.mjs        # each mode against the real contracts on mainnet forks (anvil; FORK_URL=<archive RPC>)

```

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself]
`ConfidentialPool.settle(publicValues, proof, memos)` is open to any account. The pool checks the proof
against its pinned program key, applies every effect the proof commits to, and pays each fee leg the proof
binds to `msg.sender`. Who sends a settle changes nothing else. That leaves three roles anyone can take:

- **Send a proof that is waiting** (the open board) and earn its fee.
- **Prove an op with your own Succinct prover account**, then send it yourself or post it to the board.
- **Pay for the relay's proofs** with PROVE.

To run a whole relay (take actions from pages, prove them and send them), see [RUN-A-RELAY.md](./RUN-A-RELAY.md).

API base `https://api.tacit.finance`. Every route here is public and CORS-open.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board]
A proof lands on the board in one of two ways:

- **Proved by the relay but not sent yet.** The relay sends relayed (`mode: 'settle'`) jobs itself. While
  it can't pay for a settle, it keeps proving the ones any account could send and puts them on the board.
- **Posted by its holder** with `mode: 'preproven'`.

| route | |
|---|---|
| `GET /confidential/open?limit=` | `{ pool, jobs }`, oldest first (the list can be up to five seconds old). Each job has `{ jobId, type, status, posted, publicValues, proof, memos, openSince, expiresAt, feeUsd, feeAsset }`. `status` is `open`, or `sending` while a relay has taken the job to send; a send that never finishes goes back to `open` after five minutes. `expiresAt` is in ms (0 means none). |
| `POST /confidential/landed` | `{ jobId, txHash }`. Closes the job once the API sees that the transaction succeeded, reached the pool, carries the job's public values, and that the same settle would now be refused. |
| `POST /confidential/submit` | `{ type, mode: 'preproven', publicValues, proof, memos }` posts your own proof. Its settle is simulated first, and a proof the pool would refuse now is turned away. The same public values posted twice are one job. |
| `GET /confidential/status?id=` | One job's status. An open job carries the same proof and memos as on the board. |

**What goes on the board.** Only ops whose settle is a plain `pool.settle`:

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board]
- **Never listed:**
  - router-embedded proofs: `wraptransfer`, `wraplp`, `wrapswap`, `wrapcdpmint`;
  - proofs pinned to a root that moves with the reflection: `bridgemint`, `cbtcmint`, `fastlane`;
  - adaptor-swap legs (`adaptorlock`, `adaptorclaim`, `adaptorrefund`): when one lands is part of the swap;
  - exits that carry an L2 recipe for the relay to activate.
- **Leaving the board:** a relayed job stays until its own deadline. A posted proof also leaves after a day if
  nobody sent it. A landing closes every job on the board that carries the same proof.

**Reading a job's fee.** `publicValues` is `abi.encode(PublicValues)` of the struct in
[`ConfidentialPool.sol`](../contracts/src/ConfidentialPool.sol).

- Word 0 is the tuple offset.
- Head word 8 points to `fees`, a list of `{ bytes32 assetId, uint256 value }` in the pool's units. Multiply
  `value` by the asset's `unitScale` from [`confidential-deployments.js`](../dapp/confidential-deployments.js).
- Head word 16 is the settle `deadline` in unix seconds (0 means none).

[`worker/src/confidential-open.js`](../worker/src/confidential-open.js) reads these fields and builds the call.

**The board on Nostr.** The same proofs are also posted to public Nostr relays (`wss://relay.damus.io`,
`wss://nos.lol`, `wss://relay.primal.net`, `wss://offchain.pub`), so the board does not depend on this API.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > The open board]
- **Who posts them:** holders whose page proved an action for anyone to send, /prove/ tabs, and
  `community-runner` copying this API's board.
- **The event:** kind 30078 with tags `t` = `tacit-board-v1`, `d` = `tacit-board-v1:<sha256 of the public values>`,
  a NIP-40 `expiration` and a NIP-13 `nonce` (12 bits of work). The content is JSON
  `{ v: 1, chainId, pool, type, publicValues, proof, memos, expiresAt }`.
- **The keys:** each post is signed with a key made for it alone.
- **Checking:** [`dapp/nostr-board.js`](../dapp/nostr-board.js) posts, reads and checks them. Trust nothing in a post:
  simulate the settle before sending.

**Running a relayer.** [`worker-relay/src/open-relayer.js`](../worker-relay/src/open-relayer.js) is a
complete one. It:

1. reads the board;
2. picks the oldest job whose tETH fee covers the settle's gas with a margin;
3. simulates the settle;
4. sends it through Flashbots Protect, so a reverting copy is never mined and the calldata stays private
   until it lands;
5. reports the landing.

```sh
cd worker-relay && npm ci
RELAYER_KEY=0x… RPC_URL=https://… node src/open-relayer.js     # MARGIN_BPS=2000 POLL_SECS=15 ONCE=1
```

[`tools/community-runner.mjs settles`](../tools/community-runner.mjs) does the same from the repository root with no
`worker-relay` install, beside the header and proof modes ([COMMUNITY-OPS.md](./COMMUNITY-OPS.md)).

`open-relayer.js` is the smallest one: it reads this API and counts tETH fees only.
[`tools/community-runner.mjs`](../tools/community-runner.mjs) `settles` also reads the Nostr board and counts TAC
fees ([COMMUNITY-OPS.md](./COMMUNITY-OPS.md)).

Other senders take jobs too, Tacit's relay among them. Simulate before every send: if you lose the race,
the cost is that simulation, not a reverted transaction.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account]
Tacit's relay proves on the [Succinct prover network](https://docs.succinct.xyz/docs/sp1/prover-network/quickstart)
and pays for it from its own prover account. You can do the same from yours. Then nothing depends on the
relay's queue or credit, and your op's witness goes from your machine to the network only.

1. **Fund the account.** Deposit PROVE into the network's vApp
   (`SuccinctVApp.deposit`, `0x5Ad5Bc4B18f7c173DcE17A57682Cb0Dc8788951F`; PROVE is
   `0x6BEF15D938d4E72056AC92Ea4bDD0D76B1C4ad29`).
   - The deposit credits the account that sends it. The account must be an EOA, because the network
     checks requests with `ecrecover`.
   - The network credits the deposit once indexed, which takes up to about five minutes. The minimum is
     0.01 PROVE.
   - A groth16 request needs about 1 PROVE on hand and spends about 0.4.
2. **Prove the op.** Use the same `{ type, op, memos }` a page sends to `/confidential/submit`. The op
   builders in `confidential-pool-ux.js` and the fixtures in `contracts/sp1/confidential/fixtures/` show
   each type's shape. The `exec-<op>` binary for the type proves it.
3. **Send it, or post it.**
   - Send `settle()` from any account; you are paid the fee legs you bound, so a fee you set comes back to you.
   - Or post the proof to the board, and whoever sends it is paid that fee.

[`worker-relay/src/self-prove.js`](../worker-relay/src/self-prove.js) does all three:

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account]
```sh
cd worker-relay && npm ci
export NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY=0x… RPC_URL=https://…
node src/self-prove.js deposit 5                  # approve + deposit 5 PROVE for this key's account
node src/self-prove.js prove job.json --send      # prove with your credit, then settle from SETTLE_KEY (default: the same key)
node src/self-prove.js prove job.json --post      # prove, then put it on the open board
```

**The prover binaries.** These are the Linux x86-64 builds in the `prover-bins` release that
[`worker-relay/Dockerfile`](../worker-relay/Dockerfile) names. They embed the pool's pinned guest, and
`self-prove.js` checks each one against `worker-relay/prover/bin/SHA256SUMS` before running it.

- On another system, build the relay image and run the script inside it:
  `docker build -t tacit-relay worker-relay` then
  `docker run --rm -e NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY -e RPC_URL -v "$PWD:/job" tacit-relay node src/self-prove.js prove /job/job.json --post`.
- To build them yourself, use
  [`contracts/sp1/confidential/build-all-network.sh`](../contracts/sp1/confidential/build-all-network.sh).

**Who sees the witness.** The network request carries it as a private input (`private_stdin`), and `self-prove.js`
names Succinct's own prover (`0xd4fcfce0…a4f5`) as the only one that may take it (`PROVER_WHITELIST`). Only the
network's executor and that prover can read the witness; Tacit's relay never sees it. The provers that win the open
auction take private requests and do not deliver them, so a private request sent to all provers waits out its
deadline (and still pays the base fee). `PRIVATE_STDIN=0` sends a public input to any prover instead.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site]
[tacit.finance/#prove-self](https://tacit.finance/#prove-self) and the tETH page prove in the browser, with no
binaries:

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site]
- **The account.** Your Tacit account (the Ethereum account your Tacit key derives) is the requester. Its credit pays,
  and it signs each request itself.
- **Funding.**
  - **PROVE from your connected wallet:** the wallet sends PROVE to the Tacit account (only what it lacks). It then sends
    the vApp's `permitAndDeposit` with a permit the Tacit account signs.
  - **ETH:** the wallet pays ETH that zRouter swaps to PROVE for the Tacit account, then the same deposit follows.
- **Cost.** A request needs about 0.46 PROVE on hand (0.58 for liquidity ops, which may use more gas) and spends about
  0.39.
- **Privacy.** A request is private and goes to Succinct's own prover only, as above. If it is not proved by its
  deadline, nothing is sent, and the network keeps its base fee. While the network refuses private inputs
  (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, which costs nothing), the request goes with a public input instead, open to any prover, and the
  page says so as it goes and on the result. `makeSelfProver({ input: 'private' })` keeps it private only. The relay's own
  proofs go first to Tacit's prover board (below), a machine Tacit runs, where a relayed op's witness stays with Tacit; a
  proof the board does not take in time is requested from the network, with the witness as a public input while the
  network refuses private ones. A settled job's `lane` says which way it went: `board`, `network-private` or `network-public`.
- **The settle** is sent from your connected wallet.
- **The proxy.** The network's artifact store sends no CORS headers, so the page's input goes up through
  `POST /prover/upload` and the finished proof comes back through `POST /prover/download` on the API. Both forward bytes
  to the store's own hosts and keep nothing.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving with your own prover account > From the site]
The same modules work in any page or in Node:

- [`dapp/sp1-stdin.js`](../dapp/sp1-stdin.js) builds the program input for every op a page sends, byte for byte as the
  `exec-<op>` harnesses do.
- [`dapp/succinct-net.js`](../dapp/succinct-net.js) is the network client.
- [`dapp/self-prover.js`](../dapp/self-prover.js) joins them into the `prove` that `relay.useProver` takes, and builds
  the funding transactions.
- From Node, pass `proxyBase: null` (the input goes straight to the store) and an HTTP/2 `transport`. The network's RPC
  refuses HTTP/1.1.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay]
The relay can offer each settle proof to its own prover board before it asks the prover network: a machine with a
24 GB-class NVIDIA GPU pulls the program input, proves it with the pinned guest and posts the proof back, and the relay
checks the proof against the pool (the same simulated settle it runs before sending) before it uses it. A job nobody
proves in time goes to the network as before, so a worker that stops only stops helping.

| route | |
|---|---|
| `GET /prover/board` | `{ queued, claimed, proved, failed, workers: [{ name, proved, failed, bad, lastSeenSeconds, pubkey? }], lease }`, for anyone. No inputs, no proofs. `pubkey` is the compressed secp256k1 key a worker takes sealed inputs under (below). |
| `POST /prover/claim` | Worker token. `{ worker, classes }` → `{ job: { jobId, program, stdin, cycleLimit, gasLimit, deadline, leaseUntil, label } }`, or `{}`. `stdin` is base64 of the bincode `SP1Stdin`. The claim is a lease (five minutes); a worker that goes quiet loses the job to the next claim. |
| `POST /prover/result` | Worker token. `{ jobId, publicValues, proof }` (hex; `proof` as `settle()` takes it) or `{ jobId, error }`. |

**Who may prove what.** The API knows each worker by a bearer token (`PROVER_WORKER_TOKENS`, `name:token[:classes]`).
The `private` class carries a user's witness, so it goes only to workers Tacit runs or has named for it; the `public` class
is work whose input is public anyway. A proof the pool refuses counts against its worker and the job goes on to the network.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay]
**Sealed inputs.** A page can keep an op from the relay and the API altogether: it builds the program input itself
(`dapp/sp1-stdin.js`, the same bytes the relay would build), encrypts it to one worker's `pubkey` from the board
(`dapp/sealed-input.js`: secp256k1 ECDH with a one-time key, SHA-256 over the domain `tacit-sealed-input-v1`, the shared
x-coordinate and both keys, then AES-256-GCM with that domain as the associated data) and posts
`POST /confidential/submit` `{ type, mode: 'sealed', sealed: { worker, epk, iv, ct }, memos }`. The API queues the
ciphertext for that worker only; the relay offers it on the board, and the worker opens it with its key
(`prover-worker/src/main.rs`, `unseal`; the key lives in `WORKER_KEY_FILE`, made on first start and sent with each claim).
Nothing else reads the op: the relay reads the fee from the proof's own legs and holds each to the floor this API publishes
for its asset (`GET /confidential/quote`; tETH, TAC, cUSD and cBTC are priced, so a sealed op must pay its relay fee in one of
them, or it is refused), and simulates the settle as for any proof. An op that carries no fee by design (a private send's
lock) is sealed too and metered on the relay's free-settle budgets by its type at submit, as in the clear. A sealed job is never sent to the prover network: while
the worker it is sealed to has not polled in a minute the submit is refused (`503`, code `sealed_unavailable`), and one
the worker fails is failed, so the page sends it again or unsealed. The site offers this under *Prove it yourself → Seal
my actions to Tacit's prover machine*; a settled sealed job reads `sealed: true` on its status.

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Proving for the relay]
**Running a worker.** [`contracts/sp1/confidential/prover-worker/`](../contracts/sp1/confidential/prover-worker/) is the
worker: one binary that builds the CUDA prover and the proving key once, warms the Groth16 stages at start, then claims,
proves and answers one job at a time.

```sh
contracts/sp1/confidential/prover-worker/setup-box.sh      # as root on a fresh box: the toolchain, then cargo build --release
cd contracts/sp1/confidential/prover-worker
BOARD_URL=https://api.tacit.finance WORKER_TOKEN=… WORKER_NAME=gpu1 EXPECT_VKEY=<the pool's PROGRAM_VKEY> ./target/release/tacit-prover-worker
```

It needs Linux x86-64, CUDA 12, a GPU with 24 GB of memory, 8 or more CPU cores and 50 GB of RAM, and about 10 GB of disk
for the Groth16 artifacts the SDK fetches on the first proof. `run-worker.sh` in the same directory keeps the worker
running on a rented pod (restart on a crash, GPU leftovers cleaned, thread counts from the pod's CPU quota, the server
and artifacts put back after a container restart) and `restart-worker.sh` restarts it; Tacit's own worker proves an
ordinary op in about 35 s on a $0.27/h RTX A5000 with the GPU server built for Groth16 on the GPU (see `sp1-gpu/`).

chunks.title: OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Paying for the relay's proofs
chunks.text:
[OPEN-RELAYER.md > Sending and proving confidential-pool ops yourself > Paying for the relay's proofs]
Every proof Tacit's relay makes is paid in PROVE from its prover account,
`0x68575B073DE49a94e3E3ACf6F3A0d6E3b66267C7`.

- **How soon it is used.** PROVE sent there goes into the prover network within a few minutes once 2 PROVE
  or more has arrived. Smaller amounts go in at the relay's next half-hourly top-up.
- **What it buys.** About 0.4 PROVE pays for one proof.
- **Where to do it.** [tacit.finance/relay/#prove](https://tacit.finance/relay/#prove) sends PROVE, or pays
  ETH that zRouter swaps to PROVE for that account in one transaction.

chunks.title: RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay
chunks.text:
[RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay]
A relay takes a private action from a page, proves it, and sends the proof to the pool. Anyone can run one.
`ConfidentialPool.settle` is open to any account, and the pool pays every fee bound in the proof to the
account that sends it (`msg.sender`). A relay never holds user funds or spending keys. It can decline a job,
but it cannot change or redirect one: the proof fixes what happens.

tacit.finance tries Tacit's relay first. While that relay is not proving and sending, it gives new jobs to
the first listed relay that is (`relays` in [`dapp/confidential-deployments.js`](../dapp/confidential-deployments.js)).
A job a relay took is followed on that relay until it lands.

If you only want to send proofs that are already made, you do not need any of this: see
[OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md).

chunks.title: RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > What you need
chunks.text:
[RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > What you need]
- A server for the API (Node 20). Postgres is optional: without `DATABASE_URL` the queue lives in memory and is lost on restart.
- A second process for the settle relay (`worker-relay/`, Docker, about 2 GB of memory).
- An Ethereum RPC.
- A relayer key: an EOA holding ETH for gas. It receives the relay fees.
- A Succinct prover network key with PROVE deposited ([OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md#proving-with-your-own-prover-account)
  shows how to fund one). The settle relay proves on the network, so no GPU is needed.
- An https address for the API.

chunks.title: RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 1. The API
chunks.text:
[RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 1. The API]
```sh
npm ci && (cd server && npm ci)
CONFIDENTIAL_SETTLE=1 \
CONFIDENTIAL_BOX_TOKEN=<a long random string> \
PROVER_HEARTBEAT_TOKEN=<another long random string> \
DATABASE_URL=postgres://… \
PORT=8787 node server/index.mjs
```

- `CONFIDENTIAL_SETTLE=1` turns on the relay routes (`/confidential/submit`, `status`, `relay`, `open`, `landed`, `quote`).
- The two tokens are shared with the settle relay in step 2. The first gates the routes it takes jobs from. The second lets it
  report that it is up, which is what `/confidential/relay` reads.
- `CRON_DISABLED=1` leaves the API's own chain scans off. The relay routes answer without them.
- Behind a reverse proxy, set `TRUST_PROXY=1`.
- The API answers pages from the origins in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Its default (`worker/wrangler.toml`) already includes tacit.finance.

[`server/README.md`](../server/README.md) covers memory limits and health checks.

chunks.title: RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 2. The settle relay
chunks.text:
[RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 2. The settle relay]
```sh
cd worker-relay && docker build -t tacit-relay .
docker run --restart unless-stopped \
  -e WORKER_BASE=https://your-relay.example \
  -e BOX_TOKEN=<CONFIDENTIAL_BOX_TOKEN from step 1> \
  -e PROVER_HEARTBEAT_TOKEN=<the same as step 1> \
  -e RPC_URL=https://… \
  -e RELAY_KEY=0x… \
  -e NETWORK=mainnet -e CHAIN_ID=1 \
  -e POOL_ADDR=0x000000000Ed1eabD231Be41d93b719056F7febFC \
  -e SP1_PROVER=network -e NETWORK_RPC_URL=https://rpc.mainnet.succinct.xyz -e NETWORK_PRIVATE_KEY=0x… \
  -e EXPECT_VKEY=0x006cd47fd23937a6d247696cace28c22d2c6a8280447e6ac45a3571de232d6e3 \
  -e EXEC_BIN=/app/prover/bin/exec \
  tacit-relay node src/settle-relay.js
```

- The image downloads the prover binaries and checks them against `prover/bin/SHA256SUMS`.
- `EXPECT_VKEY` stops the relay at startup if a binary would make proofs the pool refuses.
- The relay checks every job's fee before proving it, and simulates every settle before sending it.
- The fee it asks for is set by `MIN_FLOOR_USD`, `OPS_MARGIN` and `BPS_CAP`.

[`worker-relay/README.md`](../worker-relay/README.md) lists every setting, how the fee is worked out, and the loop the relay runs.

Once the relay is up, `GET https://your-relay.example/confidential/relay` answers `"state":"ok"`.

chunks.title: RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 3. Listing it on tacit.finance
chunks.text:
[RUN-A-RELAY.md > Running a relay > 3. Listing it on tacit.finance]
Open a pull request that:

- adds your API's origin (for example `https://your-relay.example`, with no path) to `relays` in
  `dapp/confidential-deployments.js`;
- adds the same origin to `connect-src` in the pages that talk to the relay. `node --test tests/relay-list.test.mjs`
  names any page that is missing it.

Any page or wallet built on the same files can list relays the same way.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks]
The live pool's history, read as a chain of blocks. Ethereum orders it and its logs hold it; nothing here is decided by Tacit, and anyone can
rebuild every block and its hash from the pool's logs alone. `GET https://api.tacit.finance/prover/blocks` serves it (worker/src/tacit-chain.js),
and [tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) draws it.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Blocks
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Blocks]
A block is one Ethereum transaction that changed the pool's notes: a `settle`, alone or with the deposit it consumes in the same transaction. A
deposit alone (`Wrap` with no note inserted or spent) changes no note and is not a block; it waits for the settle that consumes it.

Blocks are numbered from 0, the first such transaction after the pool's deployment, in Ethereum's order (block number, then log index).

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `height` | the block's number, 0 first |
| `ethBlock`, `tx` | the Ethereum block and transaction |
| `leaves` | the leaves inserted, in log order: `LeavesInserted` leaves, then `LockLeavesInserted` lock leaves |
| `nullifiers` | the nullifiers spent, in log order: `NullifiersSpent`, then the lock nullifiers |
| `notes`, `spent`, `deposits` | counts of note leaves, note nullifiers and `Wrap` logs in the transaction |
| `prev`, `hash` | the previous block's hash and this one's |

```
hash = keccak256(prev ‖ uint64(height) ‖ uint64(ethBlock) ‖ tx ‖ keccak256(leaves[0] ‖ leaves[1] ‖ …) ‖ keccak256(nullifiers[0] ‖ …))
```

Numbers are 8-byte big-endian, hashes and leaves 32 bytes, `prev` of block 0 is 32 zero bytes, and an empty list hashes as `keccak256("")`.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Cross-chain blocks
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Cross-chain blocks]
The pool spans two chains, and the proofs that carry state between them are blocks too. A cross-chain block is one reflection batch landing
on Ethereum (`attestBitcoinStateProven`): a proof of Bitcoin's tacit transactions up to a Bitcoin height, checked against the light relay's
headers and taken by the pool's verifier, which also folds the newest eth-state proof (Ethereum's finalized state, checked against the beacon
chain's sync committee) that carries the pool's state to the Bitcoin side. Each batch continues the last: its proof starts from the digest
the pool holds and ends at a new one, so the batches chain inside the proofs themselves.

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `digest` | the reflection digest the batch ends at (the pool's `knownReflectionDigest` once it lands) |
| `bitcoin` | the Bitcoin height the batch takes the pool to |
| `ethereum` | the eth-state proof it folds: its digest and the beacon slot it was finalized at |
| `tx`, `ethBlock` | the Ethereum transaction and block it landed in |
| `by` | who proved the batch, when a board worker did (a community address, or Tacit's GPU) |

`GET /prover/blocks` serves the newest as `cross`, and tacit prove draws them among the settles by the Ethereum block they landed in.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Checkpoints
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Checkpoints]
Once a day the pool's snapshot on IPFS carries a checkpoint, and the text record `tacit.snapshot` of snapshot.tacit.wei names it:

| Part | What it is | Checked against |
|---|---|---|
| `eth` | an Ethereum block and its hash | any Ethereum node |
| `tacit` | the newest block above at or before it: its height and hash | rebuilding the chain from the pool's logs |
| `trees` | the note, lock and position trees' counts and roots | the pool's storage at that block |
| `bitcoin` | the light relay's tip, and the reflection the pool holds: its digest, Bitcoin height and block | the pool's and the relay's storage |
| `ethereum` | the newest eth-state proof folded: its digest, finalized slot and the execution state root it proves | a beacon node: the slot's execution state root |

The execution state root is what makes the rest checkable from proofs alone: any value of the pool (a tree root, a count, whether a given
nullifier is spent) is checked against it with one storage proof (`eth_getProof`), and the root itself is the sync committee's, carried by a
proof the Bitcoin side checks inside its own.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Who proved a block
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Who proved a block]
A block names its prover when a community prover made the proof of one of its notes: the proof pool records, for each proof it takes, the
leaf it inserts and the address its points went to (`proof-pool.js minedBy`). That block shows the address and the points the proof earned,
paid in TAC by the points service (points × the day's most per point). Proofs made any other way, including by Tacit's own provers, name
nobody. A cross-chain block names its prover the same way, from the board (`prover-board.js`, the Bitcoin-state program).

Between proofs the same machines mine deploy salts: CreateX salts that only Tacit's deployer can use, for addresses with leading zero bytes
(`salt-pool.js`). They share what the day's proofs leave of the mining campaign's daily points.

chunks.title: POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Roles, now and next
chunks.text:
[POOL-BLOCKS.md > The pool's blocks > Roles, now and next]
- **Holders** prove what holds their key on their own device (the stage of a staged swap, a send): no one else ever sees it.
- **Provers** prove what holds no secret (deposits, presses, batches of deposits) and are paid in TAC for each proof the pool takes:
  tacit-prover on a laptop today, GPUs for the work that must be fast next.
- **Relays** send proved settles to Ethereum and are paid the settle's fee. Anyone may: `settle` takes any caller with a valid proof. A prover
  may run one too; the open board (`GET /confidential/open`) is what a relay reads.
- **Bitcoin provers** prove the reflection batches, the cross-chain blocks (large GPUs, `prove-gpu.sh`), and are paid in TAC for each one
  the relay takes from the board.

The aim is a network: every role taken by whoever shows up, Tacit's own provers and relay one participant among them, and in time not needed.
A chain whose blocks anyone can rebuild, and whose block producers are named by what they proved, is what a rollup of Tacit's own would need
first; the block format above is meant to carry over unchanged.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks]
A validity rollup for one asset, TAC. Spenders prove their own spends on their own devices (the Bitcoin shielded pool's Halo2 circuit,
unchanged); a block program checks a whole block of them in one SP1 run; Ethereum checks one Groth16 proof, holds the TAC, and takes the
block's data. Nothing in it has an owner or an upgrade key: the program, the verifier and the contract are fixed at deployment, and a new
design is a new chain that users move to through the confidential pool (V1) in one transaction.

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| Block program (SP1 guest) | `contracts/sp1/confidential/tacit-block/{guest,common}` |
| Landing contract | `contracts/src/TacitBlocks.sol` |
| Whose turn it is (TAC stakers) | `contracts/src/TacitSeats.sol` |
| Replays the chain, builds blocks | `contracts/sp1/confidential/tacit-block/node` |
| Wallet formats | `dapp/tacit-chain-lock.js`, `dapp/tacit-chain-memo.js` (vectors: `tests/vectors/`) |

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Notes and spends
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Notes and spends]
The spend relation is `btc-pool-halo2`'s: two inputs, three outputs, one asset, a deposit and an exit as BabyJubJub Pedersen
commitments, owner signatures over a body hash. `leaf = Poseidon(asset, v, npk, rho)`, `nullifier = Poseidon(nk, leaf, index)`; a note's
keys come from a 33-byte shared secret `s` its sender and recipient both derive (`btc-pool-zk.js` `outputKeys` / `ownedKeys`). The asset
is TAC alone: `SHA-256("tacit-btc-pool-zk-asset-v1" ‖ token) mod r`. TAC amounts are `u64` counts of **UNIT = 10^-8 TAC** (10^10 of the
token's smallest units), the unit the confidential pool and Bitcoin count TAC in. A note's value is a count of **shares** (below).

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Shares and fees
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Shares and fees]
Notes count shares of the chain's pool. The state keeps `pool` (the TAC behind every note, in units) and `shares`; a share is worth
`(pool + V) / (shares + V)` units, `V = 10^8` (a virtual TAC of each, which no note holds: no deposit or burn can set the price alone, and
what is left in a pool with no shares is not the next depositor's). Every spend in a block is priced at the rate before the block.

* **In.** A deposit's opening is shares; its `amount` (TAC) must buy them at the rate (wallets pay 2 bps over, which stays with the pool).
* **Out.** An exit's, hop's or migration's opening is shares; its `amount` (TAC paid out) is at most their worth less the exit fee:
  `EXIT_FEE_BPS = 10` (0.1%, rounded up) and at least `MIN_POOL_FEE = 200,000` units (0.002 TAC).
* **Payments.** A spend of notes must use its exit slot: an exit, hop, lock, migration, or a **pool share** (`OP_POOL`, 4), shares worth
  at least `MIN_POOL_FEE` that end. A lock's claim or refund note is worth the lock less `lock_fee` (0.1% of its shares, at least one).
* What stays (fees, pool shares, margins) raises every share's worth: holders earn pro rata from what others pay, and no balance is
  shown. The rate only rises. Public word 18 carries `pool ‖ shares` after the block, and the contract requires its pool to equal the TAC
  it holds for the notes (`inChain`).
* The deposit's and exit's amounts are in the body the owners sign: no one between them and the block can change what crosses the edge.

A spend's **body** is what its owners sign. Which kind it is, is fixed by what its data names:

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Shares and fees
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Shares and fees]
* a payment: `"tacit-block-body-v1" ‖ chain ‖ 3 output leaves ‖ 3 memo hashes ‖ exit address ‖ deposit amount ‖ exit amount ‖ salt`;
* an operation: `"tacit-block-op-body-v1" ‖ chain ‖ 3 output leaves ‖ 3 memo hashes ‖ op ‖ deposit amount ‖ exit amount ‖ salt`, the exit's
  value going into the operation instead of to an address (amounts u64 big-endian, zero for none).

`chain = SHA-256("tacit-block-chain-v1" ‖ chain id ‖ contract)`: derived by the contract, so a spend made for one deployment is void on
any other. The block program checks every body, every opening of a deposit or exit, and that no note is spent twice.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Operations
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Operations]
* **Hop** (`OP_HOP`, 1): the exit's value is a deposit into the confidential pool for the note `commit` names there. The block publishes
  `asset ‖ value ‖ commit` (96 bytes). Anyone sends it on with `sendHop` / `sendHops`, which calls the pool's `wrap`: the pool burns the TAC
  (it is TAC's minter) and records the deposit. No address of the spender's is in between.
* **Lock** (`OP_LOCK`, 2): the exit's value is put in a leaf of the note tree no spend proof can open, with terms `recipient (BIP-340 key) ‖
  deadline ‖ claimTo ‖ refundTo`. Before the deadline the recipient **claims** it with a BIP-340 signature over
  `SHA-256("tacit-block-claim-v1" ‖ chain ‖ leaf)`, and the block makes the `claimTo` note and publishes the signature; from the deadline
  anyone **refunds** it, making the `refundTo` note. A lock is spent once, by a nullifier in the same tree. This is the chain's half of the
  fast bridge's adaptor swap: the recipient pre-signs its claim adapted to the swap's point T, and the signature the block publishes gives
  the other leg's party the secret `t = s - s~`. A block names a time and lands only within `TIME_WINDOW` (1 h) of it; a claim is taken while
  `time + TIME_WINDOW <= deadline`, a refund from `time >= deadline`. Forced, a claim is posted at least `FORCE_DELAY + WINDOW + TIME_WINDOW`
  and a day before its deadline (the chain must reach it, then prove and land a block early enough), and a refund from `TIME_WINDOW` after
  it; the swap's other leg leaves the same headroom on its own timelock.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Operations
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Operations]
* **Migrate** (`OP_MIGRATE`, 3): the exit's value moves to a successor chain the spender names (`to`, its landing contract), for a
  note `note` names there (the successor's own commitment, opaque here). The block publishes the move as `to ‖ SHA-256("tacit-block-
  migrate-v1" ‖ to ‖ note ‖ value)` (52 bytes: the item binds the value and hides it, `note` carrying randomness) and, per successor,
  only the block's total to it; the landing contract sends each total to its successor as the block lands and keeps the hash of the
  block's moves (`migrationsOf(height)`) and each successor's total (`migrated(height, to)`). A successor makes a note from a move
  once it is shown a list with that hash, the move's position in it and the note and value its item binds, using each (height,
  position) once and making no more from a block than its total there. The spend
  proves its notes are among all of this chain's, so a migrated note keeps this chain's anonymity set and its amount stays hidden
  (a block's total to a successor shows what moved there in that block, so a wallet moves in a block others move in too). This is how
  a future chain (post-quantum proofs, or one that does what the confidential pool does) takes users and their privacy with it, with
  no owner or upgrade key: each user names the successor of their own notes.

The chain has no pools or liquidity of its own: swaps and liquidity happen in the confidential pool, where this chain's value arrives by a hop.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > A block
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > A block]
Input: the state, the block's own spends and settles (claims and refunds), the time, an optional blob buffer, and the next entries of the
forced queue (below), with the builder's answers about them. The state is the note tree (Poseidon, depth 32), the nullifier tree (indexed,
SHA-256), the last 32 note roots, the chain binding and the queue's position. The program verifies every proof in **one pairing** (a random
linear combination), applies the block, and commits nineteen 32-byte words:

| # | word | | # | word |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | state digest before | | 8 | exits hash (tag 5) |
| 1 | state digest after | | 9 | spend relation (its key's hash) |
| 2 | note root before | | 10 | queue position after |
| 3 | note root after | | 11 | queue hash after |
| 4 | new notes hash (leaf ‖ memo hash, tag 1) | | 12 | hops hash (tag 6) |
| 5 | nullifiers hash (tag 2) | | 13 | claims hash (tag 7) |
| 6 | old anchors hash (tag 3) | | 14 | the block's time |
| 7 | deposits hash (tag 4) | | 15 | blobs hash (zero in calldata mode) |
| | | | 16 | migrations hash (tag 8) |
| | | | 17 | successors' totals hash (tag 9) |
| | | | 18 | 16 zero bytes ‖ pool ‖ shares (u64 each) |

Every list is `SHA-256("tacit-block-list-v1" ‖ tag ‖ count ‖ items)`, sorted, so a list's order says nothing of which spend an item came from.
Anyone can rebuild the chain's state from the lists alone (`tacit-block-node replay`).

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)]
Only the leader of the current turn may land until `WINDOW` seconds pass with no block, or until a queued entry has waited `FORCE_DELAY +
WINDOW` (leaders that land only the entries they must cannot hold the queue back); then anyone may. Turns (`TacitSeats`) are TAC stakers
drawn by the epoch's seed: the beacon chain's randomness (`prevrandao`) in the first block of the epoch's first `SEED_BLOCKS` (4) in which
anyone keeps it, which a leader does as the epoch begins. A block hash would not do (its builder can try as many as it likes); this way the
most anyone chooses is which of four blocks keeps it, and an epoch whose seed no one kept in time has no leader, so anyone may land in it. The contract checks the proof, that the block extends the held state, the time, the queue, and:

* **Calldata mode** (word 15 = 0): the new notes and memos, nullifiers and claims are in the call, each list checked against its hash.

* **Blob mode** (word 15 != 0): they are in the transaction's blobs. The program builds the data stream, and for each blob (KZG commitment

  `C`) evaluates the blob's polynomial at `z = SHA-256(C ‖ SHA-256(stream)) mod r` itself; it commits SHA-256 of every (versioned hash, `z`,

  `y`). The contract checks each versioned hash is the transaction's blob and that `C` opens to `y` at `z` (the point-evaluation precompile):

  two polynomials that agree at a point drawn after both were fixed are the same, so the blobs hold exactly the stream. The leader picks

  the mode per block, whichever costs less. Blob data is pruned by Ethereum after about 18 days, so wallets and indexers must keep or fetch

  an archive; calldata is kept for good.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)]
* Deposits, exits, hops and anchors are always in calldata, since the contract acts on them. A deposit taken in must have been made on L1,

  bound to the shield spend that takes it in, and a spend takes in one deposit ever (its deposit's nullifier, `Poseidon(tag, C, body)`,

  enters the nullifier tree); an exit is credited to its address (`withdraw` sends it on, by anyone). The contract keeps what the chain's

  notes are worth (`inChain`: deposits' amounts taken in, less exits, hops and migrations paid out) and refuses a block that would take out

  more, or whose pool is not that, whatever its proof.

* **Deposits.** `deposit(shares, amount, C, body)` takes approved TAC (records are asset ‖ shares ‖ C ‖ body ‖ amount, 192 bytes). An

  **inbox** takes TAC with no approval and no call: `inbox(shares, amount, C, body, back)` is a CREATE2 address the confidential pool's

  unwrap (which only mints to an address) or anyone pays, and `sweep` (the leader's, or anyone's) takes it in. `sweepWithPermit` takes it

  from a holder with no ETH: the holder's ERC-2612 permit names the inbox, the inbox pulls what it lacks when it is created, and the

  caller, who pays the gas, takes the permit's `fee`. Anyone may queue the one spend that takes a swept deposit in; if none does within 7 days, `giveBack` wraps it into the

  confidential pool for `back`, and a sweep that finds the spend's key already held by another deposit wraps it there at once. An inbox is

  created once: what is paid to it after its sweep stays there.

* **Hops** are sent by anyone (`sendHop(s)`); one the confidential pool refuses (it takes a commitment once) stays, to be sent again, and

  wallets use a fresh commitment for each.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Landing (`TacitBlocks.land`)]
**Forced inclusion.** Anyone posts a spend (or a claim or refund) to the queue with `force`. Every block takes the queue's next entries in
order, the program taking each sound one and passing over the rest, and a block lands only if it reaches every entry posted `FORCE_DELAY`
or more before (or takes `MAX_FORCED`). So a leader cannot keep a spend out and go on landing, and when leaders stop landing anyone may.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Memos
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Memos]
Every note is published with a 1,152-byte memo whatever it holds. The program and contract see only its hash and length; what is inside is
the wallets' business. The wallets' memo (`tacit-chain-memo.js`) is hybrid: an ML-KEM-768 ciphertext (1,088) ‖ a secp256k1 ephemeral key
(33) ‖ the value, encrypted (8) ‖ a tag (16) ‖ 7 random bytes, and the shared secret `s` hashes in BOTH exchanges. So an attacker who
later breaks elliptic curves cannot read a recorded memo, compute a note's keys or nullifiers, or link a note to its owner without also
breaking ML-KEM. A wallet recovers its notes from its seed and the published memos alone.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders]
A wallet (`dapp/tacit-chain-wallet.js`) builds a spend from a seed: the body, the notes with their hybrid memos, each input's EdDSA signature
and the Halo2 proof (the pool's wasm prover, 17-24 s a spend in Node), padded to two output notes so every spend adds the same number of
leaves. It submits to a leader (`POST /spend`), which checks the proof natively, that the spend's asset is TAC, that its root is one a block ended
at, and that a trial block takes it; it finds its notes by trying every published memo (`scan`), which costs a hybrid decapsulation each (8 ms in
pure JS: a wallet recovered from its seed at 100k notes takes minutes, so a WASM ML-KEM and workers are the wallet's to add; no protocol change).
A shield first makes the deposit on L1 (`TacitBlocks.deposit`), whose commitment and body hash the wallet's spend names; a leader includes a
shield only once its deposit is waiting there.

A leader (`tacit-leader/`) admits only what can land: a block that held a spend of another asset, a deposit not on L1 or a root no block ended at
would revert and could be made to by anyone. Its `/build` and `/landed` routes are its own.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders > A leader's API
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders > A leader's API]
What a wallet uses is public, served by the leader's node (`tacit-block-node`; the live one is https://tacit-chain-leader.onrender.com):

* `GET /state`: height, state digest, note root, counts, the forced queue's position, the chain binding, and `pool` and `shares` (the rate a
  deposit buys at and an exit pays at).
* `GET /notes?from=N&limit=M`, `/path/N`, `/spent/0x…`, `/leaf/0x…`, `/receipt/ID`, `/mempool`: what a wallet scans and follows.
* `GET /fee`: `{ address, fee, sweepFee, shieldCap, at, window }`. A spend pays `fee` (units of 1e-8 TAC) in a note to `address`, the leader's
  chain address. `sweepFee` (TAC's own wei) is what a shield paid by permit adds on top, for the leader to send it in (`sweepWithPermit`):
  the gas of the sweep at the base fee and TAC's price, with a margin. `shieldCap` (units) is the most one shield may deposit through this
  leader for now, the launch cap. A quote is honoured for `window` seconds.
* `POST /spend` (a spend, with `back` for a shield paid to its inbox and `permit` for one paid by permit), `POST /settle`, `POST /address`
  and `GET /address/<hash>` (the chain lane's directory), and `POST /forced`: the bytes `TacitBlocks.force` takes for a spend no leader takes.
* `POST /address` with `key` and `sig` also keeps the address under a Tacit key: `sig` is the key's signature over
  SHA-256("tacit-chain-key-v1" ‖ key ‖ address), checked by the leader. `GET /address/key/<key>` returns `{ address, sig }`, so a Tacit address
  from before the chain (it carries the key, not the chain lane) is paid on the chain; the payer checks the signature again.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders > A leader's API
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > Wallets and leaders > A leader's API]
What waits lives in the leader's memory: a restart drops it, and wallets hand their kept spends over again the next time they open. Nothing
is lost, as a deposit or a paid inbox waits on Ethereum; a leader replays every landed block from the contract's events when it starts.

chunks.title: TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > What each party sees
chunks.text:
[TACIT-BLOCKS.md > The tacit chain: private TAC in blocks > What each party sees]
* **Everyone**: deposits, exits and hops (amounts and addresses, on Ethereum), the count of notes and nullifiers per block, the time.
* **Not the public**: which spend made which note, any amount inside the chain, who paid whom.
* **A block's prover**: each spend's nullifiers beside its output leaves, within one block. A nullifier cannot be tied to the leaf it spends
  without its owner's key, so this is less than Zcash shows the whole world. It never sees keys, values or owners.
* **Quantum**: hidden amounts and note linkage hold (above). Proof forgery does not: Halo2-KZG and the Groth16 wrap are pairing-based, as is
  Ethereum's verifier, so the chain's soundness waits on post-quantum proofs, as every Ethereum rollup's does.

 The proofs are more than 2,016 blocks behind the relay. One batch can’t span that gap, so the pool needs a checkpoint closer to the proven block first. Anyone can call advanceReflectionAncestry(): it walks the relay’s chain back up to 2,016 blocks a call.
